- **Urgent**: Production is down or unusable for most users, or payments/data integrity are affected, with no workaround. Examples: the mobile app crashes on launch for all users, the payment gateway is failing, invitation emails stop going out to everyone.
- **High**: A major feature is broken or badly degraded and the workaround is painful. Examples: webhooks returning 500, exports coming out empty, sensitive data appearing in exports.
- **Medium**: A feature misbehaves but a reasonable workaround exists, or the customer has a how-to question that blocks them.
- **Low**: General questions, feature requests, cosmetic issues.

Agents may change the priority the customer picked, and must add a case comment explaining why.

## First-response targets (Business and Enterprise)

| Priority | Business | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|
| Urgent | 2 hours | 30 minutes |
| High | 4 hours | 2 hours |
| Medium | 1 business day | 8 hours |
| Low | 2 business days | 1 business day |

## Before you escalate

Attach the workspace ID, the affected user's email address, timestamps with timezone, and a HAR file for browser problems (see KA-0003).

article_number: KA-0018
title: API rate limits and handling HTTP 429 responses
url_name: api-rate-limits
article_type: Reference
category: API & Integrations
plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-10-08
related_cases: [CASE-1025]
summary: How Lumora API rate limits are counted (per workspace, across all tokens and integrations), which response headers to read, and how to avoid 429 errors.
---

## How limits are counted

Limits apply **per workspace per minute**, shared by **every** API token and installed integration in that workspace. This is the most common reason a customer says "we're hitting the limit even though we're within it": their own integration is sharing the allowance with other apps, such as the Salesforce connector, Zapier-style tools or a BI connector.

| Plan | Requests per minute | Burst |
|---|---|---|
| Team | 100 | 20 |
| Business | 300 | 50 |
| Enterprise | 1,000 | 200 |

Search endpoints (`/v2/search`) have a separate limit of 30 per minute on every plan.

## Response headers

Every response includes:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: the workspace's allowance
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: requests left in the current window

title: Password reset email not received

last_reviewed: 2026-09-02

summary: Why password reset emails sometimes don't arrive (spam filtering, SSO enforcement, suppression list) and how to fix each cause.
---

## Symptoms

A user requests a password reset from the sign-in page and gets no email, so they can't sign in.

## Causes and resolution

1. **Spam or quarantine filtering.** Reset emails come from `no-reply@mail.lumora.example`. Ask the user to check spam or junk, and ask their IT team to check the mail gateway quarantine. IT should allowlist the sending domain `mail.lumora.example`.
2. **SSO is enforced.** If the workspace requires SSO, Lumora does not send reset emails, because the password is managed by the identity provider. The user should sign in with **Continue with SSO** and reset their password through their company IdP.
3. **The address is on the suppression list.** After a hard bounce, Lumora stops sending to that address.

**SSO is enforced.** If the workspace requires SSO, Lumora does not send reset emails, because the password is managed by the identity provider. The user should sign in with **Continue with SSO** and reset their password through their company IdP.
3. **The address is on the suppression list.** After a hard bounce, Lumora stops sending to that address. In the Support Console, open the user and check **Email deliverability**. If it shows *Suppressed*, click **Remove from suppression list**, then have the user request the reset again.
4. **Typo or a different account email.** Confirm the exact email on the user record. Plus-addressing (`name+tag@`) is treated as a separate address.
5. **Rate limit.** The sign-in page sends at most 3 reset emails per address per hour. Ask the user to wait for the latest email and not keep clicking.

## Still not working

An Admin can send a reset link from **Settings > Members > ⋯ > Send password reset**. If that email doesn't arrive either, escalate to the Messaging team with the user's email address and the time of the attempt in UTC.

article_number: KA-0010
title: User invitation emails not being delivered
url_name: invitation-emails-not-arriving
article_type: Troubleshooting
category: Users & Permissions
plans: [Starter, Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-10-02
related_cases: [CASE-1024]
summary: How to diagnose invitations that never arrive (domain restrictions, spam filtering, suppression list, seat limits) and how to send an invite link directly instead.
---

## Symptoms

An Admin invites people from **Settings > Members > Invite**. The invitees never get the email, and the invite shows as *Pending*.

## Check first: is this affecting everyone?

If **no** invitations are arriving for **any** workspace, check the status page for an email delivery incident. If there is none, escalate as **Urgent** to the Messaging team. For a single workspace, work through the list below.

## Causes and resolution

1. **Domain restriction.** **Settings > Security > Allowed email domains** blocks invites to other domains *without showing an error*. Add the domain, or invite the user as a Guest.
2. **Spam or quarantine.** Invitations come from `invites@mail.lumora.example`. Ask IT to allowlist `mail.lumora.example`.

**Domain restriction.** **Settings > Security > Allowed email domains** blocks invites to other domains *without showing an error*. Add the domain, or invite the user as a Guest.
2. **Spam or quarantine.** Invitations come from `invites@mail.lumora.example`. Ask IT to allowlist `mail.lumora.example`. Microsoft 365 tenants with strict impersonation protection often quarantine these emails.
3. **Suppression list.** If an earlier email to that address bounced, it is suppressed. Check **Email deliverability** on the pending invite in the Support Console and remove the suppression.
4. **No seats left.** If every paid seat is in use, invites wait in *Pending — awaiting seat* and no email is sent. Add seats or free one up.
5. **SSO with JIT provisioning.** If SSO is required and just-in-time provisioning is on, no invite is needed. Users can simply sign in with SSO.

## Workaround: send the link directly

On the pending invite, click **⋯ > Copy invite link** and send it through another channel. The link is valid for 7 days and works only for the invited email address.

| Setting | Default | Configurable range | Plans |
|---|---|---|---|

| Failed attempts before lockout | 5 | 3 – 10 | Business, Enterprise |

summary: Why the Lumora–Salesforce connector loses its connection (refresh token policy, the connecting user's session or password, IP restrictions, API limits) and how to make it stable.
---

## Symptoms

The Salesforce connector shows **Disconnected — reauthorization required** every few hours or days. Syncs stop until someone reconnects it.

## Causes and resolution

1. **Refresh token policy in Salesforce.** In Salesforce Setup, go to **Connected Apps OAuth Usage > Lumora Workspace > Manage > Edit Policies**. Set **Refresh Token Policy** to *Refresh token is valid until revoked*. If it's set to "Expire refresh token after X hours", the connector disconnects on that schedule. This is the most common cause.
2. **The connecting user's password changed or they were deactivated.** The connector runs as the Salesforce user who authorized it. Use a dedicated **integration user** whose password never expires.

summary: Fixes for "Invalid verification code" when turning on or using 2FA, which is most often caused by the phone's clock being out of sync.
---

## Symptoms

The user scans the QR code in their authenticator app, types the 6-digit code, and sees **Invalid verification code**. This can happen during setup or at sign-in.

## Cause

Lumora uses time-based one-time passwords (TOTP, 30-second window, with a tolerance of one window either side). The usual causes are:

- **The phone's clock is wrong.** If it is more than about 60 seconds off, every code fails.
- **An old QR code was scanned.** Each time the setup dialog opens it creates a new secret, so a code from a previous attempt won't work.
- **The code was entered after it expired.**

## Resolution

1. On the phone, turn on automatic date and time:

**

## Resolution

1. On the phone, turn on automatic date and time:
   - iOS: **Settings > General > Date & Time > Set Automatically**
   - Android: **Settings > System > Date & time > Set time automatically**
   - Google Authenticator on Android also has **⋮ > Settings > Time correction for codes > Sync now**.
2. In the authenticator app, delete any old *Lumora* entries.
3. In Lumora, cancel the setup dialog and start again at **Profile > Security > Two-factor authentication**, scanning the **new** QR code.
4. Enter the code that is currently showing, not one that is about to expire.

## Lost device

The user signs in with one of their backup codes. If they have none, a workspace Admin can reset 2FA for them from **Settings > Members > ⋯ > Reset 2FA**. Support can only reset 2FA after verifying identity under the account recovery procedure.

## Status

**Open.** Engineering ticket ENG-4471. Fix planned for release **2026.11.1**.

## Symptoms

- A user logs out through their identity provider portal (IdP-initiated logout), but Lumora tabs that are already open keep working.
- After logout, pressing Back or reopening the app shows cached project data until the page is refreshed.

## Cause

There are two separate problems:

1. If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL**, Lumora never hears about the IdP logout. The Lumora session lasts until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
2. Even when Single Logout is set up, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout.

1. If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL**, Lumora never hears about the IdP logout. The Lumora session lasts until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
2. Even when Single Logout is set up, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout. This is the defect being fixed in 2026.11.1.

## Workarounds

1. Make sure Single Logout is configured in **both** the IdP and in Lumora (**Settings > Security > Single sign-on > Edit > Single Logout URL**). This ends the server-side session.
2. Shorten **Settings > Security > Session lifetime** to as little as 1 hour.
3. On shared or kiosk devices, turn on **Settings > Security > Disable offline cache**. Users lose offline access, but nothing is cached on the device.
4. Users can sign out with **Profile > Sign out** in Lumora as well as in the IdP. That clears the local cache.

## Customer messaging

Tell customers that server-side sessions **are** ended when Single Logout is configured. The remaining risk is data cached in the browser on that device. Link the case to ENG-4471 so the customer is notified when the fix ships.

## Work out what the second charge is

Open the customer in the Billing Console and compare the card statement with **Invoices** and **Payments**.

| What the customer sees | Likely cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| A small or matching amount marked *pending*, which disappears within 3–7 business days | A card **authorization hold** taken when the card was added or updated | Explain that it's a hold, not a charge. Nothing to refund. |
| A second, smaller charge in the same month | **Proration** after adding seats or upgrading mid-cycle | Send the proration invoice and explain the line items. |
| Two full charges, each with its own invoice number and workspace | The customer pays for **two workspaces** | Confirm with the customer. Offer to merge or cancel one (KA-0047). |

| Two full charges, each with its own invoice number and workspace | The customer pays for **two workspaces** | Confirm with the customer. Offer to merge or cancel one (KA-0047). |
| Two identical charges for the same invoice | A **true duplicate** caused by a payment retry | Refund one (below). |

## Refund a true duplicate

1. In the Billing Console, open the duplicate **payment** (not the invoice).
2. Click **Refund > Full**, reason *Duplicate*.
3. Refunds reach the card in 5–10 business days, depending on the bank.
4. Add a case comment with the refund ID.

Agents can refund duplicates without approval. Any other refund over $500 needs approval from a Billing Lead.

How to tell them apart in **Settings > Billing > Invoices**:

- The original shows the status **Void** and the invoice number ends in `-V`.
- The revision has the same base number with the suffix `-R1` and the status **Paid** or **Open**.
- Only the revised invoice is charged.

Other reasons for invoices that look alike:

- A **proration invoice** for seats added in the middle of the cycle.

- **Two workspaces** with the same billing contact (see KA-0012).

## For accounting

- Turn on **Settings > Billing > Hide voided invoices** to remove voided invoices from the list.

In most cases one of the two invoices is **void** and replaced by a **revised** invoice. Lumora creates a revision when billing details change after the invoice is issued, for example a new billing address, an added VAT/tax ID, or a change to the PO number.

How to tell them apart in **Settings > Billing > Invoices**:

- The original shows the status **Void** and the invoice number ends in `-V`.
- The revision has the same base number with the suffix `-R1` and the status **Paid** or **Open**.
- Only the revised invoice is charged.

Other reasons for invoices that look alike:

- A **proration invoice** for seats added in the middle of the cycle.

- The revision has the same base number with the suffix `-R1` and the status **Paid** or **Open**.
- Only the revised invoice is charged.

Other reasons for invoices that look alike:

- A **proration invoice** for seats added in the middle of the cycle. It has a different number and a smaller amount.
- **Two workspaces** with the same billing contact (see KA-0012).

## For accounting

- Turn on **Settings > Billing > Hide voided invoices** to remove voided invoices from the list.
- Click **Export statement** to download a CSV that contains only valid invoices and credit notes.
- If the customer needs the voided invoice removed from the record completely (for example, it was already sent to an ERP), Billing can issue a formal credit note. Escalate to the Billing queue.

summary: Steps to diagnose payment forms that stop processing payments (rotated keys, webhook secret, currency, gateway outage). This is always handled as Urgent.

## Priority

Failed payments mean the customer is losing revenue. Set the case to **Urgent**.

## Step 1: Rule out an outage

- Check `status.lumora.example` for **Forms** or **Payments**.
- Ask the customer to check their payment provider's own status page.

## Step 2: Check the payment log

In the form, open **Settings > Payments > Transaction log**. Each attempt shows the gateway's response code.

| Error in log | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `authentication_failed` / `invalid_api_key` | The API key was rotated or revoked in the gateway dashboard | Reconnect the gateway: **Settings > Integrations > Payments > Reconnect** |
| `webhook_signature_invalid` | The webhook signing secret changed | Copy the new secret into Lumora's payment settings |

- Failed submissions are saved as **Unpaid**. After the fix, the customer can send each submitter a payment link from **Responses > Unpaid > Send payment link**.

## Escalate

If the log shows `gateway_timeout` or Lumora errors (`5xx`), escalate to the Forms team on-call with the form ID and the transaction IDs.

Each attempt shows the gateway's response code.

| Error in log | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `authentication_failed` / `invalid_api_key` | The API key was rotated or revoked in the gateway dashboard | Reconnect the gateway: **Settings > Integrations > Payments > Reconnect** |
| `webhook_signature_invalid` | The webhook signing secret changed | Copy the new secret into Lumora's payment settings |
| `currency_not_supported` | The form's currency changed to one the merchant account doesn't support | Change the form currency back, or enable the currency in the gateway |
| `account_restricted` | The gateway has restricted the merchant account (verification, compliance) | The customer must resolve it with their payment provider |
| `test_mode_key_in_live` | A test key was entered on a live form | Use the live key |
| No entries at all | The form doesn't reach the payment step | Check the payment field's conditional logic |

## Step 3: Tell the customer

- Payments are processed by the customer's own payment provider. Lumora doesn't hold card data.
- Failed submissions are saved as **Unpaid**. After the fix, the customer can send each submitter a payment link from **Responses > Unpaid > Send payment link**.

## Escalate

- **Urgent**: Production is down or unusable for most users, or payments/data integrity are affected, with no workaround. Examples: the mobile app crashes on launch for all users, the payment gateway is failing, invitation emails stop going out to everyone.
- **High**: A major feature is broken or badly degraded and the workaround is painful. Examples: webhooks returning 500, exports coming out empty, sensitive data appearing in exports.
- **Medium**: A feature misbehaves but a reasonable workaround exists, or the customer has a how-to question that blocks them.
- **Low**: General questions, feature requests, cosmetic issues.

Agents may change the priority the customer picked, and must add a case comment explaining why.

## First-response targets (Business and Enterprise)

| Priority | Business | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|
| Urgent | 2 hours | 30 minutes |
| High | 4 hours | 2 hours |
| Medium | 1 business day | 8 hours |
| Low | 2 business days | 1 business day |

## Before you escalate

Attach the workspace ID, the affected user's email address, timestamps with timezone, and a HAR file for browser problems (see KA-0003).

article_number: KA-0030
title: Data connector sync is slower than usual
url_name: data-connector-sync-delays
article_type: Troubleshooting
category: API & Integrations
plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-10-07
related_cases: [CASE-1014]
summary: How to diagnose data connectors that take 30+ minutes to sync instead of the usual interval (source throttling, full resyncs, errors, plan interval).
---

## Expected interval

Incremental syncs run every **15 minutes on Team** and **5 minutes on Business and Enterprise** (KA-0001). A sync normally takes under a minute for a few thousand changed records.

## Diagnose

Open **Settings > Integrations > [connector] > Sync log**. For each run it shows the start time, duration, records processed, and any warnings.

| What the sync log shows | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `Throttled by source (429)` | The *external system* is limiting Lumora's requests | Raise the API limit in the source system, or reduce the fields being synced |
| `Full resync in progress` | A schema change or a re-authorization started a full resync | Wait. Incremental syncs resume afterwards. Large sources can take hours |

## Response headers

Every response includes:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: the workspace's allowance
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: requests left in the current window
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: when the window resets, as Unix epoch seconds

When the limit is exceeded, the API returns **429 Too Many Requests** with a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

## Best practices

1. Honor `Retry-After`, and use exponential backoff with jitter.
2. Use **webhooks** instead of polling for changes (KA-0019).
3. Use batch endpoints (`POST /v2/tasks/batch`, up to 100 items).
4. Request only the fields you need with `?fields=`.

## Investigating a complaint

**Settings > API > Usage** shows requests per token and per integration for the last 7 days. Ask the customer for a screenshot. Usually one integration is using most of the allowance. Enterprise customers can buy a higher limit through their CSM.

| `Throttled by source (429)` | The *external system* is limiting Lumora's requests | Raise the API limit in the source system, or reduce the fields being synced |
| `Full resync in progress` | A schema change or a re-authorization started a full resync | Wait. Incremental syncs resume afterwards. Large sources can take hours |
| Runs are skipped or overlap | The previous sync hadn't finished when the next was due | Reduce the objects or fields synced, or ask for a longer interval |
| `Auth error` | The connection's credentials expired | Reconnect (see KA-0031 for Salesforce) |
| Nothing unusual, but runs are long | Possibly a backlog on Lumora's side | Check the status page, then escalate |

## Reduce sync volume

- Under **Connector > Objects**, turn off objects you don't use.
- Under **Connector > Filters**, sync only active records, for example `Status != Closed`.
- Avoid formula or rollup fields in the source system that change on every record each night. They make every record look modified.

## Escalate

Include the connector type, the workspace ID, and a screenshot or export of the sync log covering the slow period.

## Symptoms

When several people edit the same board, document or task at once, each person's changes reach the others about **30 seconds** late instead of immediately. Users may also see edit conflicts.

## Cause

Lumora sends live updates over a WebSocket connection to `wss://rt.lumora.example`. If something on the network blocks or breaks WebSockets, the app quietly falls back to **polling every 30 seconds**. That matches the delay users describe. Common culprits:

- A corporate proxy or secure web gateway that doesn't support WebSocket upgrades, or that inspects TLS traffic.
- A firewall that closes idle connections after a short time.
- Browser extensions (privacy or ad-blocking tools).

## Confirm

1. In the app, open **Help > Connection diagnostics**.

## "500 errors when setting up webhooks"

First work out **who** is returning the 500:

- **The customer's endpoint returns 500** (shown in **Webhooks > Endpoint > Delivery log**). The problem is in their code. Common causes:
  - The verification `challenge` isn't handled, so their code fails trying to parse an event it doesn't expect.
  - The signature is checked against *parsed and re-serialized* JSON instead of the raw request body.

- **The Lumora API returns 500 to `POST /v2/webhooks`.** Usually the URL is invalid, isn't HTTPS, or points to a private IP address, and the API returns a 500 where it should return a 400. That is known defect ENG-4210. Check that the URL is public HTTPS with a valid certificate. If it still fails, escalate with the `X-Request-Id` from the response.

## How webhooks work

## Retention

## "500 errors when setting up webhooks"

First work out **who** is returning the 500:

- **The customer's endpoint returns 500** (shown in **Webhooks > Endpoint > Delivery log**). The problem is in their code. Common causes:
  - The verification `challenge` isn't handled, so their code fails trying to parse an event it doesn't expect.
  - The signature is checked against *parsed and re-serialized* JSON instead of the raw request body.
  - The handler does slow work before responding. Respond `200` first and process the event in the background.
- **The Lumora API returns 500 to `POST /v2/webhooks`.** Usually the URL is invalid, isn't HTTPS, or points to a private IP address, and the API returns a 500 where it should return a 400. That is known defect ENG-4210. Check that the URL is public HTTPS with a valid certificate. If it still fails, escalate with the `X-Request-Id` from the response.

## Response headers

Every response includes:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: the workspace's allowance
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: requests left in the current window
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: when the window resets, as Unix epoch seconds

When the limit is exceeded, the API returns **429 Too Many Requests** with a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

## Best practices

1. Honor `Retry-After`, and use exponential backoff with jitter.
2. Use **webhooks** instead of polling for changes (KA-0019).

Limits apply **per workspace per minute**, shared by **every** API token and installed integration in that workspace. |---|---|---|

| Business | 300 | 50 |
| Enterprise | 1,000 | 200 |

title: Browser lags when filtering tables with 100,000+ rows

## Symptoms

Filtering or sorting a table view with more than about 100,000 rows makes the browser freeze for several seconds, or shows "Page unresponsive".

## Why it happens

By default, table views load up to 100,000 rows into the browser so that quick filters respond immediately. Above that size, filtering in the browser uses a lot of memory and CPU, especially with formula columns.

## Resolution

1. **Turn on server-side filtering.** In the view, go to **View settings > Performance > Filter on server**. Filters and sorts then run on Lumora's servers and only one page of results (500 rows) is loaded. This is the main fix.
2. **Filter on indexed fields.** Status, Assignee, Created date, Due date, Project and any custom field with **Indexed** ticked (**Settings > Fields > Edit**) filter much faster.

Choose **Change role**, **Change seat**, **Deactivate** or **Remove**.

## CSV import

1. Go to **Settings > Members > Import > Download template**.
2. Fill in the columns `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `role` (`admin`, `member` or `guest`), `seat` (`full` or `viewer`), `action` (`add`, `update`, `deactivate` or `remove`) and an optional `projects` column, separated by semicolons.
3. Upload the file. Lumora shows a preview with row-level errors before anything changes.
4. Confirm. You can import up to 5,000 rows per file. Invitations go out as each row is processed.

## Deactivate or remove?

- **Deactivate** frees the seat and keeps everything the user created assigned to them. You can reverse it.
- **Remove** frees the seat and moves their open tasks to the person you choose. You can't reverse it.

## SCIM

On Enterprise, generate a token under **Settings > Security > SCIM** and enter it with the base URL `https://api.lumora.example/scim/v2` in your IdP. Users and group-to-role mappings then come from the IdP.

Filters and sorts then run on Lumora's servers and only one page of results (500 rows) is loaded. This is the main fix.
2. **Filter on indexed fields.** Status, Assignee, Created date, Due date, Project and any custom field with **Indexed** ticked (**Settings > Fields > Edit**) filter much faster. Business includes up to 20 indexed custom fields, Enterprise up to 100.
3. **Use saved views** with the filters already set, so the full table never loads.
4. **Hide formula columns** you don't need in that view.
5. **Archive old rows.** Moving completed items older than 12 months to an archive table can make the main table much smaller.

## Notes

- From release 2026.11, server-side filtering turns on automatically above 50,000 rows.

title: Reports over long date ranges take a long time to generate
url_name: slow-report-generation

category: Reports & Data
plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-09-22

summary: Why reports covering many months are slow and how to speed them up with summary mode, fewer calculated columns and cached snapshots.
---

## Symptoms

A report over a long date range (for example 6 months of task data) takes 5 to 15 minutes, or times out.

## Why it happens

Detail reports read every row in the range and work out calculated fields for each one when the report runs. These are the main costs:

- **Calculated and formula columns**, especially ones that look up data in other projects.
- **Grouping by a text field** that has many different values.
- **Including archived projects**.
- **"Status history" fields**, which read the full change log.

## Speed it up

1. **Turn on summary mode.** In the report, go to **Settings > Data source > Use daily summaries**. Summary mode reads pre-calculated daily totals. A 6-month report usually finishes in under 30 seconds. You lose row-level detail, but you can still drill into a single day.

5. **Wrong source report.** After a dashboard is duplicated, widgets still point to the *original* report. Check **Edit widget > Source**.

summary: Explains why two users can see different times in the same report, how to set a fixed report timezone, and how to fix scheduled reports that run at the wrong hour.
---

## Default behavior

Timestamps are stored in UTC and shown in **each viewer's profile timezone** (**Profile > Preferences > Timezone**). That's why users in New York and Lisbon see different times for the same task. Both are correct.

Date-only fields (for example *Due date*) have no time and are the same for everyone.

**Grouping by day** uses the viewer's timezone too. A task completed at 23:30 in New York counts as "Tuesday" for a New York viewer and "Wednesday" for a Lisbon viewer, so daily totals can differ between users.

## Make a report consistent for everyone

Open the report, go to **Settings > Timezone > Fixed**, and choose a timezone (for example *America/New_York*).

summary: How to keep very large tables responsive with server-side filtering, saved views, indexed fields and paging.
---

## Symptoms

Filtering or sorting a table view with more than about 100,000 rows makes the browser freeze for several seconds, or shows "Page unresponsive".

## Why it happens

By default, table views load up to 100,000 rows into the browser so that quick filters respond immediately. Above that size, filtering in the browser uses a lot of memory and CPU, especially with formula columns.

## Resolution

1. **Turn on server-side filtering.** In the view, go to **View settings > Performance > Filter on server**. Filters and sorts then run on Lumora's servers and only one page of results (500 rows) is loaded. This is the main fix.
2. **Filter on indexed fields.** Status, Assignee, Created date, Due date, Project and any custom field with **Indexed** ticked (**Settings > Fields > Edit**) filter much faster.

Filters and sorts then run on Lumora's servers and only one page of results (500 rows) is loaded. This is the main fix.
2. **Filter on indexed fields.** Status, Assignee, Created date, Due date, Project and any custom field with **Indexed** ticked (**Settings > Fields > Edit**) filter much faster. Business includes up to 20 indexed custom fields, Enterprise up to 100.
3. **Use saved views** with the filters already set, so the full table never loads.
4. **Hide formula columns** you don't need in that view.
5. **Archive old rows.** Moving completed items older than 12 months to an archive table can make the main table much smaller.

## Notes

- From release 2026.11, server-side filtering turns on automatically above 50,000 rows.
- If the problem continues with server-side filtering on, collect a HAR file and a browser performance profile and escalate to Frontend Engineering.

title: Salesforce connector keeps disconnecting
url_name: salesforce-connector-disconnects
article_type: Troubleshooting
category: API & Integrations
plans: [Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-10-09
related_cases: [CASE-1007]
summary: Why the Lumora–Salesforce connector loses its connection (refresh token policy, the connecting user's session or password, IP restrictions, API limits) and how to make it stable.
---

## Symptoms

The Salesforce connector shows **Disconnected — reauthorization required** every few hours or days. Syncs stop until someone reconnects it.

## Causes and resolution

1. **Refresh token policy in Salesforce.** In Salesforce Setup, go to **Connected Apps OAuth Usage > Lumora Workspace > Manage > Edit Policies**. Set **Refresh Token Policy** to *Refresh token is valid until revoked*. If it's set to "Expire refresh token after X hours", the connector disconnects on that schedule. This is the most common cause.
2. **The connecting user's password changed or they were deactivated.** The connector runs as the Salesforce user who authorized it. Use a dedicated **integration user** whose password never expires.
3.

2. **The connecting user's password changed or they were deactivated.** The connector runs as the Salesforce user who authorized it. Use a dedicated **integration user** whose password never expires.
3. **IP restrictions.** If **Permitted Users** is set to *Admin approved users are pre-authorized* or IP relaxation is set to *Enforce IP restrictions*, allow Lumora's outbound IPs (listed at `https://lumora.example/ips`) on the integration user's profile, or set **IP Relaxation** to *Relax IP restrictions* for the Lumora connected app.
4. **Salesforce API limit reached.** When the org hits its daily API limit, Salesforce rejects the calls. Lumora shows this as a disconnect. Check **Setup > Company Information > API Requests, Last 24 Hours**.
5. **Sandbox refresh.** Refreshing a sandbox removes all OAuth grants. Reconnect afterwards.
6. **Too many tokens.** Salesforce allows 5 refresh tokens per user per connected app. Authorizing more than that silently revokes the oldest one. Don't share one integration user across several Lumora workspaces.

## Reconnect

**Settings > Integrations > Salesforce > Reconnect**, signed in as the integration user. Field mappings are kept.

| `Throttled by source (429)` | The *external system* is limiting Lumora's requests | Raise the API limit in the source system, or reduce the fields being synced |
| `Full resync in progress` | A schema change or a re-authorization started a full resync | Wait. Incremental syncs resume afterwards. Large sources can take hours |
| Runs are skipped or overlap | The previous sync hadn't finished when the next was due | Reduce the objects or fields synced, or ask for a longer interval |
| `Auth error` | The connection's credentials expired | Reconnect (see KA-0031 for Salesforce) |
| Nothing unusual, but runs are long | Possibly a backlog on Lumora's side | Check the status page, then escalate |

## Reduce sync volume

- Under **Connector > Objects**, turn off objects you don't use.
- Under **Connector > Filters**, sync only active records, for example `Status != Closed`.
- Avoid formula or rollup fields in the source system that change on every record each night. They make every record look modified.

## Escalate

Include the connector type, the workspace ID, and a screenshot or export of the sync log covering the slow period.

## Status

**Open.** Engineering ticket ENG-4471. Fix planned for release **2026.11.1**.

## Symptoms

There are two separate problems:

1. If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL**, Lumora never hears about the IdP logout. The Lumora session lasts until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
2. Even when Single Logout is set up, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout.

Each attempt shows the gateway's response code.

|---|---|---|

| `currency_not_supported` | The form's currency changed to one the merchant account doesn't support | Change the form currency back, or enable the currency in the gateway |
| `account_restricted` | The gateway has restricted the merchant account (verification, compliance) | The customer must resolve it with their payment provider |
| `test_mode_key_in_live` | A test key was entered on a live form | Use the live key |
| No entries at all | The form doesn't reach the payment step | Check the payment field's conditional logic |

## Step 3: Tell the customer

- Payments are processed by the customer's own payment provider. Lumora doesn't hold card data.
- Failed submissions are saved as **Unpaid**. After the fix, the customer can send each submitter a payment link from **Responses > Unpaid > Send payment link**.

title: Backup retention and restoring deleted data

article_type: Policy
category: Security & Compliance
plans: [Starter, Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-09-08
related_cases: [CASE-1027]
summary: How long Lumora keeps backups, what users can restore themselves (trash, version history), and how to request a restore from backup.
---

## Backup policy

- Lumora takes encrypted snapshots of all workspace data **every 24 hours**, plus continuous transaction logs, in a separate region from production.
- **Retention:** 30 days (Starter, Team, Business). 90 days (Enterprise).
- Backups are for disaster recovery and restoring a whole workspace or project. They are not an archive the customer can browse.

## What users can restore themselves

| What | Where | How long |
|---|---|---|
| Deleted tasks, files, projects | **Trash** | 30 days |
| Earlier versions of a file or document | **Version history** on the item | Depends on the version setting (KA-0016) |
| Deleted custom fields | **Settings > Fields > Deleted** | 30 days |
| Field changes on a task | **Activity** tab, then **Revert** | Unlimited |

| Deleted tasks, files, projects | **Trash** | 30 days |
| Earlier versions of a file or document | **Version history** on the item | Depends on the version setting (KA-0016) |
| Deleted custom fields | **Settings > Fields > Deleted** | 30 days |
| Field changes on a task | **Activity** tab, then **Revert** | Unlimited |

## Requesting a restore from backup

For anything not covered above (for example a project bulk-edited by mistake, or data deleted more than 30 days ago but still within the backup window):

1. A workspace **Owner** must ask for it in writing on the case.
2. Give the project or workspace name and a point in time (date, time and timezone) to restore to.
3. Restores are done **into a new copy of the project**, never over live data. The customer then copies back what they need.
4. Target time: 2 business days (Enterprise: 1 business day). There is no charge on Business and Enterprise. On Starter and Team, the first restore each year is free.

## Customer-side backups

Customers can set up their own regular exports with scheduled reports (KA-0024) or the bulk export API (`POST /v2/exports`).

## How it should work

Admins mark a custom field as **Sensitive** in **Settings > Fields > Edit > Sensitive**. Sensitive fields:

- Are masked in the UI (`••••`) for users without the **View sensitive data** permission.
- Are **left out of all exports** (manual, scheduled and API bulk export) unless the person running the export has **Export sensitive data**.
- Are recorded in the audit log whenever someone reveals or exports them.

## Known issue (resolved)

| | |
|---|---|
| Ticket | ENG-4388 |
| Affected releases | 2026.08.1 to 2026.09.1 |
| Fixed in | **2026.09.2** (released 2026-09-16) |

## What counts as a run?

One run is one rule triggering once, however many actions it carries out. Some examples:

- A rule that runs when a task's status changes, and posts a comment and sends an email, counts as **1 run**.
- A scheduled rule that updates 200 tasks counts as **200 runs** (one per task).
- Runs where the conditions aren't met **don't** count.

## What happens at the limit?

- **Active rules:** You can't activate another rule until one is paused.
- **Monthly runs:** Owners get an email at 80% and 100%. At 100%, rules stop running until the next billing month. Paid plans can buy run packs (+25,000) under **Settings > Billing > Add-ons**.

## Other limits

- Rules can call each other up to 10 levels deep. After that, the chain is stopped to prevent loops.
- Each scheduled rule can process up to 5,000 items per run.
- See usage under **Settings > Automations > Usage**.

Date-only fields (for example *Due date*) have no time and are the same for everyone.

title: Real-time collaboration changes appear with a delay
url_name: realtime-collaboration-delay

category: Performance
plans: [Starter, Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-09-26
related_cases: [CASE-1032]
summary: Changes from other users showing up about 30 seconds late almost always means WebSockets are blocked and the app has fallen back to polling. Here is how to confirm and fix it.
---

## Symptoms

When several people edit the same board, document or task at once, each person's changes reach the others about **30 seconds** late instead of immediately. Users may also see edit conflicts.

## Cause

Lumora sends live updates over a WebSocket connection to `wss://rt.lumora.example`. If something on the network blocks or breaks WebSockets, the app quietly falls back to **polling every 30 seconds**. That matches the delay users describe. Common culprits:

- A corporate proxy or secure web gateway that doesn't support WebSocket upgrades, or that inspects TLS traffic.
- A firewall that closes idle connections after a short time.
- Browser extensions (privacy or ad-blocking tools).

## Confirm

1. In the app, open **Help > Connection diagnostics**.

Admins can add more people to these alerts: **Settings > Notifications > Workspace alerts > Storage**.

## What happens at 100%

New uploads and new file versions are blocked. Everything else, including viewing and downloading existing files, keeps working.

## Free up space

1. **Empty the trash.** Deleted files count until they are purged (30 days, or right away with **Empty trash**).
2. **Limit file versions.** In **Settings > Files > Version history**, keep the last 10 versions instead of all of them.
3. Use **Usage > Storage > Largest files** to find large files and delete or archive them.
4. Archived projects still count. Export the project and delete it if it's no longer needed.

title: Google Calendar two-way sync isn't working

plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-09-19
related_cases: [CASE-1016]
summary: How to fix Lumora events and task due dates not appearing in Google Calendar, or Google events not appearing in Lumora.
---

## How the sync works

- Each user connects their own Google account under **Profile > Integrations > Google Calendar**.
- **Lumora → Google:** tasks with a due date and time, and Lumora events, are written to one chosen calendar (by default a new calendar called *Lumora*).
- **Google → Lumora:** events from the calendars you tick show up on your Lumora calendar view.
- Changes usually sync within 2 minutes.

## Troubleshooting

1. **Looking at the wrong calendar.** Lumora items go to the *Lumora* calendar, not the user's primary calendar. In Google Calendar, make sure the *Lumora* calendar is visible (ticked in the left sidebar).
2. **Tasks without a time.** Tasks with only a due date are added as all-day events only if **Sync all-day tasks** is on.
3.

In Google Calendar, make sure the *Lumora* calendar is visible (ticked in the left sidebar).
2. **Tasks without a time.** Tasks with only a due date are added as all-day events only if **Sync all-day tasks** is on.
3. **Google calendars not ticked.** Under **Profile > Integrations > Google Calendar > Calendars to show**, tick the calendars that should appear in Lumora.
4. **Permission not granted.** If the user unticked calendar permissions on Google's consent screen, the sync works in only one direction. Disconnect, reconnect, and grant every requested permission.
5. **Google Workspace admin restrictions.** The customer's Google admin may block third-party apps. They need to allow *Lumora Workspace* under **Admin console > Security > API controls > App access control**.
6. **Token revoked.** A password change or Google security review can revoke access. The integration page then shows **Reconnect required**.

## Escalate

If the integration shows **Connected** and the steps above don't help, collect the user's email, an example item (its title and time, with timezone), and the direction of sync that fails. Escalate to the Integrations team.

| `Throttled by source (429)` | The *external system* is limiting Lumora's requests | Raise the API limit in the source system, or reduce the fields being synced |
| `Full resync in progress` | A schema change or a re-authorization started a full resync | Wait. Incremental syncs resume afterwards. Large sources can take hours |
| Runs are skipped or overlap | The previous sync hadn't finished when the next was due | Reduce the objects or fields synced, or ask for a longer interval |
| `Auth error` | The connection's credentials expired | Reconnect (see KA-0031 for Salesforce) |
| Nothing unusual, but runs are long | Possibly a backlog on Lumora's side | Check the status page, then escalate |

## Reduce sync volume

- Under **Connector > Objects**, turn off objects you don't use.
- Under **Connector > Filters**, sync only active records, for example `Status != Closed`.
- Avoid formula or rollup fields in the source system that change on every record each night. They make every record look modified.

## Escalate

Include the connector type, the workspace ID, and a screenshot or export of the sync log covering the slow period.

## Backup policy

- Lumora takes encrypted snapshots of all workspace data **every 24 hours**, plus continuous transaction logs, in a separate region from production.
- **Retention:** 30 days (Starter, Team, Business). 90 days (Enterprise).
- Backups are for disaster recovery and restoring a whole workspace or project. They are not an archive the customer can browse.

## What users can restore themselves

## Enterprise Organizations

An **Organization** groups several Enterprise workspaces under one admin console.

1. An Organization Admin turns on **Org settings > Collaboration > Shared projects**.
2. In any workspace, a project manager clicks **Project > ⋯ > Share with workspaces** and chooses the target workspaces.
3. Members of those workspaces see the project in their own sidebar with their normal role, without becoming guests.
4. Reports and dashboards can include shared projects. Automations run in the workspace that **owns** the project.

## Limitations

- Shared projects can't be moved between workspaces. Ownership stays with the original workspace.
- Custom fields only from the owning workspace appear in a shared project.
- To combine two workspaces permanently, ask Support for a **workspace merge** (Enterprise, planned with the CSM).

## Symptoms

A user requests a password reset from the sign-in page and gets no email, so they can't sign in.

## Causes and resolution

1. **Spam or quarantine filtering.** Reset emails come from `no-reply@mail.lumora.example`. Ask the user to check spam or junk, and ask their IT team to check the mail gateway quarantine. IT should allowlist the sending domain `mail.lumora.example`.
2. **SSO is enforced.** If the workspace requires SSO, Lumora does not send reset emails, because the password is managed by the identity provider. The user should sign in with **Continue with SSO** and reset their password through their company IdP.
3. **The address is on the suppression list.** After a hard bounce, Lumora stops sending to that address.

| Single Logout URL (optional) | `https://<subdomain>.lumora.example/sso/saml/slo` |
| NameID format | `emailAddress` |
| Required attributes | `email`, `firstName`, `lastName` |

## Steps in Lumora

1. Go to **Settings > Security > Single sign-on > Add SAML connection**.
2. Upload the IdP metadata XML, **or** paste the SSO URL, the IdP entity ID and the X.509 signing certificate.
3. Click **Test connection** in a private browser window.
4. When the test passes, choose the enforcement level: **Optional** or **Required for verified domains**.

Keep at least one Owner account able to sign in with a password ("break-glass") until you've confirmed SSO works.

## Common errors

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Audience mismatch` | The entity ID in the IdP doesn't match exactly | Copy the value again. It is case-sensitive and must have no trailing slash |
| `Signature validation failed` | The certificate was rotated or the wrong one was pasted | Upload fresh IdP metadata |
| `Assertion expired` | The IdP server's clock is off | Fix NTP on the IdP. Allowed skew is 3 minutes |

If the workspace requires SSO, that's actually the expected behavior — Lumora does **not** send password reset emails in that case, because the password is managed by the company's identity provider (IdP), not by Lumora.

## What to tell the user

- The password for this workspace isn't stored in Lumora, so there's no "reset" email to send once SSO is required.

## Symptoms

A user requests a password reset from the sign-in page and gets no email, so they can't sign in.

## Causes and resolution

1. **Spam or quarantine filtering.** Reset emails come from `no-reply@mail.lumora.example`. Ask the user to check spam or junk, and ask their IT team to check the mail gateway quarantine. IT should allowlist the sending domain `mail.lumora.example`.
2. **SSO is enforced.** If the workspace requires SSO, Lumora does not send reset emails, because the password is managed by the identity provider. The user should sign in with **Continue with SSO** and reset their password through their company IdP.
3. **The address is on the suppression list.** After a hard bounce, Lumora stops sending to that address.

**SSO is enforced.** If the workspace requires SSO, Lumora does not send reset emails, because the password is managed by the identity provider. The user should sign in with **Continue with SSO** and reset their password through their company IdP.
3. **The address is on the suppression list.** After a hard bounce, Lumora stops sending to that address. In the Support Console, open the user and check **Email deliverability**. If it shows *Suppressed*, click **Remove from suppression list**, then have the user request the reset again.
4. **Typo or a different account email.** Confirm the exact email on the user record. Plus-addressing (`name+tag@`) is treated as a separate address.
5. **Rate limit.** The sign-in page sends at most 3 reset emails per address per hour. Ask the user to wait for the latest email and not keep clicking.

## Still not working

An Admin can send a reset link from **Settings > Members > ⋯ > Send password reset**. If that email doesn't arrive either, escalate to the Messaging team with the user's email address and the time of the attempt in UTC.

title: User invitation emails not being delivered

summary: How to diagnose invitations that never arrive (domain restrictions, spam filtering, suppression list, seat limits) and how to send an invite link directly instead.
---

## Symptoms

An Admin invites people from **Settings > Members > Invite**. The invitees never get the email, and the invite shows as *Pending*.

## Check first: is this affecting everyone?

If **no** invitations are arriving for **any** workspace, check the status page for an email delivery incident. If there is none, escalate as **Urgent** to the Messaging team. For a single workspace, work through the list below.

## Causes and resolution

1. **Domain restriction.** **Settings > Security > Allowed email domains** blocks invites to other domains *without showing an error*. Add the domain, or invite the user as a Guest.
2. **Spam or quarantine.** Invitations come from `invites@mail.lumora.example`. Ask IT to allowlist `mail.lumora.example`.

**Domain restriction.** **Settings > Security > Allowed email domains** blocks invites to other domains *without showing an error*. Add the domain, or invite the user as a Guest.
2. **Spam or quarantine.** Invitations come from `invites@mail.lumora.example`. Ask IT to allowlist `mail.lumora.example`. Microsoft 365 tenants with strict impersonation protection often quarantine these emails.
3. **Suppression list.** If an earlier email to that address bounced, it is suppressed. Check **Email deliverability** on the pending invite in the Support Console and remove the suppression.
4. **No seats left.** If every paid seat is in use, invites wait in *Pending — awaiting seat* and no email is sent. Add seats or free one up.
5. **SSO with JIT provisioning.** If SSO is required and just-in-time provisioning is on, no invite is needed. Users can simply sign in with SSO.

## Workaround: send the link directly

On the pending invite, click **⋯ > Copy invite link** and send it through another channel. The link is valid for 7 days and works only for the invited email address.

category: Sign-in & Security
plans: [Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-10-12
related_cases: [CASE-1049]
summary: After logging out through the identity provider, Lumora sessions and cached data can stay on the device. Workarounds are available, and a fix is planned for release 2026.11.1.
---

## Status

**Open.** Engineering ticket ENG-4471. Fix planned for release **2026.11.1**.

## Symptoms

- A user logs out through their identity provider portal (IdP-initiated logout), but Lumora tabs that are already open keep working.
- After logout, pressing Back or reopening the app shows cached project data until the page is refreshed.

## Cause

There are two separate problems:

1. If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL**, Lumora never hears about the IdP logout. The Lumora session lasts until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
2. Even when Single Logout is set up, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout.

| Single Logout URL (optional) | `https://<subdomain>.lumora.example/sso/saml/slo` |
| NameID format | `emailAddress` |
| Required attributes | `email`, `firstName`, `lastName` |

## Steps in Lumora

1. Go to **Settings > Security > Single sign-on > Add SAML connection**.
2. Upload the IdP metadata XML, **or** paste the SSO URL, the IdP entity ID and the X.509 signing certificate.
3. Click **Test connection** in a private browser window.
4. When the test passes, choose the enforcement level: **Optional** or **Required for verified domains**.

Keep at least one Owner account able to sign in with a password ("break-glass") until you've confirmed SSO works.

## Common errors

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Audience mismatch` | The entity ID in the IdP doesn't match exactly | Copy the value again. It is case-sensitive and must have no trailing slash |
| `Signature validation failed` | The certificate was rotated or the wrong one was pasted | Upload fresh IdP metadata |
| `Assertion expired` | The IdP server's clock is off | Fix NTP on the IdP. Allowed skew is 3 minutes |

It is case-sensitive and must have no trailing slash |

| `Email not in verified domain` | The user's email domain hasn't been claimed | Verify the domain under **Domains** |

## OIDC

OIDC setup is under **Add OIDC connection**. The redirect URI is `https://<subdomain>.lumora.example/sso/oidc/callback`.

## How limits are counted

Limits apply **per workspace per minute**, shared by **every** API token and installed integration in that workspace. This is the most common reason a customer says "we're hitting the limit even though we're within it": their own integration is sharing the allowance with other apps, such as the Salesforce connector, Zapier-style tools or a BI connector.

| Plan | Requests per minute | Burst |
|---|---|---|
| Team | 100 | 20 |
| Business | 300 | 50 |
| Enterprise | 1,000 | 200 |

Search endpoints (`/v2/search`) have a separate limit of 30 per minute on every plan.

## Response headers

Every response includes:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: the workspace's allowance
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: requests left in the current window

4. If your endpoint returns anything other than 2xx, or takes longer than 10 seconds, Lumora retries 5 times over 24 hours with exponential backoff. After 24 hours of failures, the endpoint is **disabled**.

## "500 errors when setting up webhooks"

First work out **who** is returning the 500:

- **The customer's endpoint returns 500** (shown in **Webhooks > Endpoint > Delivery log**). The problem is in their code. Common causes:
  - The verification `challenge` isn't handled, so their code fails trying to parse an event it doesn't expect.
  - The signature is checked against *parsed and re-serialized* JSON instead of the raw request body.
  - The handler does slow work before responding. Respond `200` first and process the event in the background.
- **The Lumora API returns 500 to `POST /v2/webhooks`.** Usually the URL is invalid, isn't HTTPS, or points to a private IP address, and the API returns a 500 where it should return a 400. That is known defect ENG-4210. Check that the URL is public HTTPS with a valid certificate. If it still fails, escalate with the `X-Request-Id` from the response.

## Re-enable a disabled endpoint

Fix the endpoint, then click **Re-enable**.

summary: After logging out through the identity provider, Lumora sessions and cached data can stay on the device. Workarounds are available, and a fix is planned for release 2026.11.1.

## Status

**Open.** Engineering ticket ENG-4471. Fix planned for release **2026.11.1**.

## Symptoms

- A user logs out through their identity provider portal (IdP-initiated logout), but Lumora tabs that are already open keep working.
- After logout, pressing Back or reopening the app shows cached project data until the page is refreshed.

## Cause

There are two separate problems:

1. If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL**, Lumora never hears about the IdP logout. The Lumora session lasts until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
2. Even when Single Logout is set up, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout.

1. If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL**, Lumora never hears about the IdP logout. The Lumora session lasts until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
2. Even when Single Logout is set up, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout. This is the defect being fixed in 2026.11.1.

## Workarounds

1. Make sure Single Logout is configured in **both** the IdP and in Lumora (**Settings > Security > Single sign-on > Edit > Single Logout URL**). This ends the server-side session.
2. Shorten **Settings > Security > Session lifetime** to as little as 1 hour.
3. On shared or kiosk devices, turn on **Settings > Security > Disable offline cache**. Users lose offline access, but nothing is cached on the device.
4. Users can sign out with **Profile > Sign out** in Lumora as well as in the IdP. That clears the local cache.

## Customer messaging

Tell customers that server-side sessions **are** ended when Single Logout is configured. The remaining risk is data cached in the browser on that device. Link the case to ENG-4471 so the customer is notified when the fix ships.

| Category | Example events |

Q06.answer:
This is a known, currently **open** issue (KA-0008: "Known issue: SSO logout does not fully end the Lumora session"), not yet fixed — a fix is planned for release **2026.11.1** via engineering ticket ENG-4471.

## Why it happens
There are two separate problems causing already-open tabs to keep working after an IdP (e.g., Okta) logout:
- If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL** configured, Lumora never finds out about the Okta logout, so the session simply runs until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
- Even when Single Logout *is* configured so the server-side session properly ends, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout — this is the specific defect targeted for the 2026.11.1 fix.

## Workarounds available now
- Configure Single Logout in **both** Okta and Lumora (**Settings > Security > Single sign-on > Edit > Single Logout URL**) — this ends the server-side session.
- Shorten **Settings > Security > Session lifetime** to as little as 1 hour.
- On shared/kiosk devices, turn on **Settings > Security > Disable offline cache** so nothing is cached locally (users lose offline access).
- Have users also sign out via **Profile > Sign out** inside Lumora in addition to logging out of Okta — this clears the local cache.

## Customer messaging note
You can tell customers that the server-side session *is* properly ended once Single Logout is configured — the remaining risk is just data cached in the browser on that device. It's worth linking their case to ENG-4471 so they're notified automatically when the fix ships.

## Symptoms

When several people edit the same board, document or task at once, each person's changes reach the others about **30 seconds** late instead of immediately. Users may also see edit conflicts.

## Cause

Lumora sends live updates over a WebSocket connection to `wss://rt.lumora.example`. If something on the network blocks or breaks WebSockets, the app quietly falls back to **polling every 30 seconds**. That matches the delay users describe. Common culprits:

- A corporate proxy or secure web gateway that doesn't support WebSocket upgrades, or that inspects TLS traffic.
- A firewall that closes idle connections after a short time.
- Browser extensions (privacy or ad-blocking tools).

## Confirm

1. In the app, open **Help > Connection diagnostics**.

When a user's role shows **Admin** but everything they see is read-only, work through these checks in order:

1. **Seat type (check this first).** Seat type takes priority over role — a user on a **Viewer seat** is read-only everywhere even if their role says Admin. Go to **Settings > Members**, find the user, and if **Seat** says *Viewer*, change it to *Full* (this requires a free paid seat).
2. **Wrong workspace.** The user may belong to several workspaces and only be an Admin in one of them. Have them switch workspaces using the picker in the top-left corner.
3. **Billing lock.** If the subscription is past due, the entire workspace becomes read-only for everyone except Owners.
4. **Stale session.** Role changes only take effect the next time the page loads — ask the user to sign out and back in.
5. **SCIM group mapping (Enterprise only).** If roles are managed through the IdP via SCIM, any role change made directly in Lumora gets overwritten at the next sync. In that case, the group-to-role mapping needs to be changed in the IdP instead.

Since **seat type overrides role**, the Viewer seat check is almost always the culprit and the right place to start.

Q08.answer:
This happens because **all of the paid seats on your workspace are currently in use**. When there are no seats left, new invitations are created in a *Pending — awaiting seat* state, and Lumora deliberately does **not** send the invitation email until a seat becomes available.

## How to fix it

- **Add more seats** to your plan, or
- **Free up an existing seat** — for example by deactivating or removing a user who no longer needs access — which will let the pending invite(s) send automatically.

Once a seat is available, the invite moves out of "Pending — awaiting seat" and the invitation email goes out.

## If you need access right away

If you can't wait for a seat to free up, this specific "awaiting seat" state isn't one where a direct invite link workaround applies the same way as other delivery issues (domain restrictions, spam quarantine, suppression lists) — the invite literally won't be sent until a seat exists. The fastest resolution is to add a seat or deactivate/reassign an unused one.

## Other possible causes (if seats are *not* the issue)

If you check and seats are actually available, but invites still don't arrive, the other common causes are:

| Cause | What happens | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Domain restriction | Blocks invites to other domains silently, no error shown | Add the domain in Settings > Security > Allowed email domains, or invite as Guest |
| Spam/quarantine | Mail gateway blocks emails from `invites@mail.lumora.example` | Ask IT to allowlist `mail.lumora.example` |
| Suppression list | A prior bounce suppressed the address | Check "Email deliverability" on the pending invite and remove the suppression |
| SSO with JIT provisioning | No invite needed — users just sign in via SSO | No action needed |

If this is affecting **every** workspace (not just one), check the status page for an email delivery incident, and if none is listed, this should be escalated as Urgent to the Messaging team.

Q10.answer:
No refund is needed in this case. When a customer adds or updates a card, Lumora's payment processor places a temporary **authorization hold** on the card to verify it — this shows up as a small or matching "pending" charge that has no invoice because it's not an actual charge, just a hold.

Here's how to confirm and respond:

- **Check the amount and status**: compare what the customer sees on their card statement against **Invoices** and **Payments** in the Billing Console.
- **Confirm it's a hold**: if it's a small or matching pending amount with no corresponding invoice, it's an authorization hold, not a real charge.
- **What happens next**: these holds typically disappear on their own within **3–7 business days**.
- **What to tell the customer**: explain that it's just a hold from the bank verifying the card, nothing has actually been charged, and there is nothing to refund.

If instead you find it's a *real* charge — for example, a second full charge tied to its own invoice (could mean a second workspace) or two identical charges against the same invoice (a true duplicate from a payment retry) — those are handled differently: a second workspace charge should be confirmed with the customer (with an option to merge/cancel), while a true duplicate charge should be refunded via **Billing Console > open the duplicate payment > Refund > Full**, reason "Duplicate". But for a standard pending authorization hold after a card update, no refund action is required since no money has actually moved.

## Work out what the second charge is

Open the customer in the Billing Console and compare the card statement with **Invoices** and **Payments**.

| What the customer sees | Likely cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| A small or matching amount marked *pending*, which disappears within 3–7 business days | A card **authorization hold** taken when the card was added or updated | Explain that it's a hold, not a charge. Nothing to refund. |
| A second, smaller charge in the same month | **Proration** after adding seats or upgrading mid-cycle | Send the proration invoice and explain the line items. |
| Two full charges, each with its own invoice number and workspace | The customer pays for **two workspaces** | Confirm with the customer. Offer to merge or cancel one (KA-0047). |

| Two full charges, each with its own invoice number and workspace | The customer pays for **two workspaces** | Confirm with the customer. Offer to merge or cancel one (KA-0047). |
| Two identical charges for the same invoice | A **true duplicate** caused by a payment retry | Refund one (below). |

## Refund a true duplicate

1. In the Billing Console, open the duplicate **payment** (not the invoice).
2. Click **Refund > Full**, reason *Duplicate*.
3. Refunds reach the card in 5–10 business days, depending on the bank.
4. Add a case comment with the refund ID.

Agents can refund duplicates without approval. Any other refund over $500 needs approval from a Billing Lead.

## Question

"I see the same invoice twice in billing history. Will I be billed twice, and what should our accounting team use?"

## Answer

In most cases one of the two invoices is **void** and replaced by a **revised** invoice. Lumora creates a revision when billing details change after the invoice is issued, for example a new billing address, an added VAT/tax ID, or a change to the PO number.

How to tell them apart in **Settings > Billing > Invoices**:

- The original shows the status **Void** and the invoice number ends in `-V`.
- The revision has the same base number with the suffix `-R1` and the status **Paid** or **Open**.
- Only the revised invoice is charged.

Other reasons for invoices that look alike:

- A **proration invoice** for seats added in the middle of the cycle.

- The revision has the same base number with the suffix `-R1` and the status **Paid** or **Open**.
- Only the revised invoice is charged.

Other reasons for invoices that look alike:

- A **proration invoice** for seats added in the middle of the cycle. It has a different number and a smaller amount.
- **Two workspaces** with the same billing contact (see KA-0012).

## For accounting

- Turn on **Settings > Billing > Hide voided invoices** to remove voided invoices from the list.
- Click **Export statement** to download a CSV that contains only valid invoices and credit notes.
- If the customer needs the voided invoice removed from the record completely (for example, it was already sent to an ERP), Billing can issue a formal credit note. Escalate to the Billing queue.

Q12.answer:
No, you won't be charged twice. This is expected behavior, not a billing error.

## Why you see two invoices

Lumora creates a **revised invoice** whenever billing details change after an invoice is first issued — for example, a new billing address, an added VAT/tax ID, or a change to the PO number.

| Invoice | Suffix | Status | Charged? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original | `-V` | **Void** | No — it's cancelled |
| Revision | `-R1` | **Paid** or **Open** | Yes — this is the one you're billed for |

So the `-V` invoice is the voided original, and the `-R1` invoice with the same base number is its replacement. **Only the `-R1` (revised) invoice is actually charged**.

## For your accounting records

If you'd like a cleaner record without voided invoices cluttering the list:

- Turn on **Settings > Billing > Hide voided invoices** to filter them out of the invoice list.
- Use **Export statement** to download a CSV containing only valid invoices and credit notes.
- If you've already sent the voided invoice to an ERP system and need it formally removed, Lumora's Billing team can issue a credit note — this requires escalating to the Billing queue.

If what you're actually seeing is two *separate* charges (rather than a void/revision pair), that's usually either a proration charge for seats added mid-cycle, or two workspaces sharing the same billing contact — let me know if that's the case and I can walk through how to distinguish those instead.

title: Using the audit log for compliance
url_name: audit-log-compliance
article_type: Reference
category: Security & Compliance
plans: [Business, Enterprise]

summary: Which user and admin actions the audit log records, how long it keeps them, and how to export or stream it to a SIEM.
---

## What is recorded

| Category | Example events |
|---|---|
| Authentication | Sign-in success and failure, SSO assertion, 2FA turned on or reset, lockout, sign-out |
| Members and roles | Invite, role change, seat change, deactivate, SCIM changes |
| Data access | Sensitive field revealed, export started and downloaded, file downloaded (Enterprise) |
| Content | Project or task created, updated, deleted, restored, or permission changed |
| Admin settings | Security policy, SSO, integrations, API tokens, webhooks |
| Billing | Plan change, payment method change |

Each entry records who did it (the user or the API token), the IP address, the user agent, the time in UTC, the object, and the values before and after.

## Retention

- **Business:** 1 year, viewable in the app.
- **Enterprise:** 7 years.

## What counts as a run?

One run is one rule triggering once, however many actions it carries out. Some examples:

- A rule that runs when a task's status changes, and posts a comment and sends an email, counts as **1 run**.
- A scheduled rule that updates 200 tasks counts as **200 runs** (one per task).
- Runs where the conditions aren't met **don't** count.

## What happens at the limit?

- **Active rules:** You can't activate another rule until one is paused.
- **Monthly runs:** Owners get an email at 80% and 100%. At 100%, rules stop running until the next billing month. Paid plans can buy run packs (+25,000) under **Settings > Billing > Add-ons**.

## Other limits

- Rules can call each other up to 10 levels deep. After that, the chain is stopped to prevent loops.
- Each scheduled rule can process up to 5,000 items per run.
- See usage under **Settings > Automations > Usage**.

## Step 1: Rule out an outage

## Step 2: Check the payment log

In the form, open **Settings > Payments > Transaction log**. Each attempt shows the gateway's response code.

|---|---|---|
| `authentication_failed` / `invalid_api_key` | The API key was rotated or revoked in the gateway dashboard | Reconnect the gateway: **Settings > Integrations > Payments > Reconnect** |
| `webhook_signature_invalid` | The webhook signing secret changed | Copy the new secret into Lumora's payment settings |

- Failed submissions are saved as **Unpaid**. After the fix, the customer can send each submitter a payment link from **Responses > Unpaid > Send payment link**.

## Escalate

If the log shows `gateway_timeout` or Lumora errors (`5xx`), escalate to the Forms team on-call with the form ID and the transaction IDs.

Each attempt shows the gateway's response code.

| Error in log | Cause | Fix |

## Step 3: Tell the customer

- Failed submissions are saved as **Unpaid**. After the fix, the customer can send each submitter a payment link from **Responses > Unpaid > Send payment link**.

## Escalate

- **Urgent**: Production is down or unusable for most users, or payments/data integrity are affected, with no workaround. Examples: the mobile app crashes on launch for all users, the payment gateway is failing, invitation emails stop going out to everyone.
- **High**: A major feature is broken or badly degraded and the workaround is painful. Examples: webhooks returning 500, exports coming out empty, sensitive data appearing in exports.
- **Medium**: A feature misbehaves but a reasonable workaround exists, or the customer has a how-to question that blocks them.
- **Low**: General questions, feature requests, cosmetic issues.

Agents may change the priority the customer picked, and must add a case comment explaining why.

## First-response targets (Business and Enterprise)

Q14.answer:
Yes, that's a known gap in the current system — not a bug specific to your workspace. According to Lumora's storage alert documentation:

- Alerts are normally sent at **80%** (to Owners and billing contacts), **95%** (to Owners, billing contacts and Admins), and **100%** (to everyone, shown as an error when uploading).
- However, there's a **documented known gap**: if storage usage jumps from below 80% straight to 100% in a single day — exactly the scenario you describe with a large bulk import — only the 100% message is triggered. The 80% and 95% thresholds get skipped because the checks don't catch rapid, large jumps within the same check interval.
- A fix (a daily check designed to catch this kind of jump) is planned for release in **2026.11**.

So in short: missing the 80%/95% warnings after a big bulk import is expected behavior given the current known limitation, not a malfunction. At 100%, new uploads and new file versions are blocked, but viewing and downloading existing files continues to work normally. If you need to free up space in the meantime, you can empty the trash, limit file version history, identify large files under Usage > Storage > Largest files, or remove unneeded archived projects — or upgrade the plan / buy additional storage packs.

summary: How to diagnose data connectors that take 30+ minutes to sync instead of the usual interval (source throttling, full resyncs, errors, plan interval).
---

## Expected interval

Incremental syncs run every **15 minutes on Team** and **5 minutes on Business and Enterprise** (KA-0001). A sync normally takes under a minute for a few thousand changed records.

## Diagnose

Open **Settings > Integrations > [connector] > Sync log**. For each run it shows the start time, duration, records processed, and any warnings.

| What the sync log shows | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `Throttled by source (429)` | The *external system* is limiting Lumora's requests | Raise the API limit in the source system, or reduce the fields being synced |
| `Full resync in progress` | A schema change or a re-authorization started a full resync | Wait. Incremental syncs resume afterwards. Large sources can take hours |

| Payment fails | Right away, then on days 3, 7 and 12 |
| Auto-renew turned off | 30, 7 and 1 day before expiry |

## What happens when payment fails?

1. **Days 0–14 (grace period):** Everything works. A banner is shown to Owners.
2. **After day 14:** The workspace becomes **read-only** for everyone except Owners, who can still reach billing.
3. **After day 60:** The workspace is suspended. Data is kept for 90 more days, then deleted.

## Restore access

An Owner updates the payment method under **Settings > Billing > Payment method** and clicks **Retry payment**. Access comes back within a minute of a successful charge.

## If the customer had no warning

- Check the billing contacts and the email suppression status (see KA-0004).
- Agents can grant a **7-day courtesy extension** once per 12 months from the Billing Console (**Subscription > Extend grace**).

## What counts as a run?

One run is one rule triggering once, however many actions it carries out. Some examples:

- A rule that runs when a task's status changes, and posts a comment and sends an email, counts as **1 run**.
- A scheduled rule that updates 200 tasks counts as **200 runs** (one per task).
- Runs where the conditions aren't met **don't** count.

## What happens at the limit?

- **Active rules:** You can't activate another rule until one is paused.
- **Monthly runs:** Owners get an email at 80% and 100%. At 100%, rules stop running until the next billing month. Paid plans can buy run packs (+25,000) under **Settings > Billing > Add-ons**.

## Other limits

- Rules can call each other up to 10 levels deep. After that, the chain is stopped to prevent loops.
- Each scheduled rule can process up to 5,000 items per run.
- See usage under **Settings > Automations > Usage**.

## Requesting a restore from backup

For anything not covered above (for example a project bulk-edited by mistake, or data deleted more than 30 days ago but still within the backup window):

Q15.answer:
On the **Business** plan, the maximum file size you can upload via the web (browser) or mobile app is **250 MB**.

If you need to go bigger than that, you have a few options:

- **Use the API for resumable uploads** – Business plan supports resumable uploads via the API (`POST /v2/files/uploads`, sent in 8 MB chunks) up to **1 GB**.
- **Link instead of uploading** – Attach a file from a connected cloud drive (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Box) using **Attach > From cloud storage**. Linked files don't count against storage or the size limit, so there's effectively no size cap this way.
- **Compress or split the file** – e.g., zip up a folder of images to get under the limit.
- **Upgrade to Enterprise** – which raises the web/mobile upload limit to **2 GB** and the API resumable upload limit to **5 GB**.

Note that Support cannot manually raise the upload limit — it's tied to the plan, so upgrading or using one of the workarounds above are the only ways to go bigger.
