## Symptoms

Filtering or sorting a table view with more than about 100,000 rows makes the browser freeze for several seconds, or shows "Page unresponsive".

## Why it happens

By default, table views load up to 100,000 rows into the browser so that quick filters respond immediately. Above that size, filtering in the browser uses a lot of memory and CPU, especially with formula columns.

## Resolution

1. **Turn on server-side filtering.** In the view, go to **View settings > Performance > Filter on server**. Filters and sorts then run on Lumora's servers and only one page of results (500 rows) is loaded. This is the main fix.
2. **Filter on indexed fields.** Status, Assignee, Created date, Due date, Project and any custom field with **Indexed** ticked (**Settings > Fields > Edit**) filter much faster.

Filters and sorts then run on Lumora's servers and only one page of results (500 rows) is loaded. This is the main fix.
2. **Filter on indexed fields.** Status, Assignee, Created date, Due date, Project and any custom field with **Indexed** ticked (**Settings > Fields > Edit**) filter much faster. Business includes up to 20 indexed custom fields, Enterprise up to 100.
3. **Use saved views** with the filters already set, so the full table never loads.
4. **Hide formula columns** you don't need in that view.
5. **Archive old rows.** Moving completed items older than 12 months to an archive table can make the main table much smaller.

## Notes

- From release 2026.11, server-side filtering turns on automatically above 50,000 rows.
- If the problem continues with server-side filtering on, collect a HAR file and a browser performance profile and escalate to Frontend Engineering.

## Firefox

1. Press **F12** and open **Network**. Tick **Persist Logs**.
2. Reproduce the problem.
3. Click the gear icon and choose **Save All As HAR**.

## Safari

1. Turn on **Develop** in **Settings > Advanced > Show features for web developers**.
2. Choose **Develop > Show Web Inspector > Network**, tick **Preserve Log**, and reproduce.
3. Click **Export**.

## Privacy

HAR files can contain session cookies. Ask customers to upload them through the secure attachment link on the case, never by email. Support deletes attachments 30 days after the case closes.

## Supported browsers

The latest two major versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. Internet Explorer and legacy Edge are not supported.

Q16.answer:
Even though your own integration sends about 80 requests a minute—under the Team plan's 100/minute limit—the limit isn't per integration, it's **per workspace, shared by every API token and installed integration** in that workspace. So you can still hit 429 errors if other apps or tokens in the same workspace (e.g., a Salesforce connector, Zapier-style tool, or BI connector) are also making calls and pushing the combined total over the limit.

A few other things that can contribute:

- **Search endpoints** (`/v2/search`) have their own separate limit of 30 requests/minute on every plan, regardless of your overall workspace allowance.
- The Team plan allows **100 requests/minute with a burst of 20**, so a short spike above the steady 80/min (even from your own integration) could trigger a 429 if it coincides with other traffic.

## How to confirm and fix it

1. Check the response headers on your calls: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` tell you the workspace's allowance and how much is left in the current window.
2. Go to **Settings > API > Usage** to see requests per token and per integration over the last 7 days — this usually reveals that one integration (possibly not yours) is consuming most of the shared allowance.
3. When you do get a 429, honor the `Retry-After` header and use exponential backoff with jitter.
4. Where possible, switch from polling to **webhooks**, use the batch endpoint (`POST /v2/tasks/batch`, up to 100 items), and request only the fields you need with `?fields=` to reduce the number of calls.

## How limits are counted

Limits apply **per workspace per minute**, shared by **every** API token and installed integration in that workspace. This is the most common reason a customer says "we're hitting the limit even though we're within it": their own integration is sharing the allowance with other apps, such as the Salesforce connector, Zapier-style tools or a BI connector.

| Business | 300 | 50 |
| Enterprise | 1,000 | 200 |

Search endpoints (`/v2/search`) have a separate limit of 30 per minute on every plan.

## Response headers

- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: requests left in the current window

article_number: KA-0030
title: Data connector sync is slower than usual
url_name: data-connector-sync-delays
article_type: Troubleshooting
category: API & Integrations
plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-10-07
related_cases: [CASE-1014]
summary: How to diagnose data connectors that take 30+ minutes to sync instead of the usual interval (source throttling, full resyncs, errors, plan interval).
---

## Expected interval

Incremental syncs run every **15 minutes on Team** and **5 minutes on Business and Enterprise** (KA-0001). A sync normally takes under a minute for a few thousand changed records.

## Diagnose

Open **Settings > Integrations > [connector] > Sync log**. For each run it shows the start time, duration, records processed, and any warnings.

| What the sync log shows | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `Throttled by source (429)` | The *external system* is limiting Lumora's requests | Raise the API limit in the source system, or reduce the fields being synced |
| `Full resync in progress` | A schema change or a re-authorization started a full resync | Wait. Incremental syncs resume afterwards. Large sources can take hours |

## Response headers

Every response includes:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: the workspace's allowance
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: requests left in the current window
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: when the window resets, as Unix epoch seconds

When the limit is exceeded, the API returns **429 Too Many Requests** with a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

## Best practices

1. Honor `Retry-After`, and use exponential backoff with jitter.
2. Use **webhooks** instead of polling for changes (KA-0019).
3. Use batch endpoints (`POST /v2/tasks/batch`, up to 100 items).
4. Request only the fields you need with `?fields=`.

## Investigating a complaint

**Settings > API > Usage** shows requests per token and per integration for the last 7 days. Ask the customer for a screenshot. Usually one integration is using most of the allowance. Enterprise customers can buy a higher limit through their CSM.

| `Throttled by source (429)` | The *external system* is limiting Lumora's requests | Raise the API limit in the source system, or reduce the fields being synced |
| `Full resync in progress` | A schema change or a re-authorization started a full resync | Wait. Incremental syncs resume afterwards. Large sources can take hours |
| Runs are skipped or overlap | The previous sync hadn't finished when the next was due | Reduce the objects or fields synced, or ask for a longer interval |
| `Auth error` | The connection's credentials expired | Reconnect (see KA-0031 for Salesforce) |
| Nothing unusual, but runs are long | Possibly a backlog on Lumora's side | Check the status page, then escalate |

## Reduce sync volume

- Under **Connector > Objects**, turn off objects you don't use.
- Under **Connector > Filters**, sync only active records, for example `Status != Closed`.
- Avoid formula or rollup fields in the source system that change on every record each night. They make every record look modified.

## Escalate

Include the connector type, the workspace ID, and a screenshot or export of the sync log covering the slow period.

article_number: KA-0029
title: Real-time collaboration changes appear with a delay
url_name: realtime-collaboration-delay
article_type: Troubleshooting
category: Performance
plans: [Starter, Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-09-26
related_cases: [CASE-1032]
summary: Changes from other users showing up about 30 seconds late almost always means WebSockets are blocked and the app has fallen back to polling. Here is how to confirm and fix it.
---

## Symptoms

When several people edit the same board, document or task at once, each person's changes reach the others about **30 seconds** late instead of immediately. Users may also see edit conflicts.

## Cause

Lumora sends live updates over a WebSocket connection to `wss://rt.lumora.example`. If something on the network blocks or breaks WebSockets, the app quietly falls back to **polling every 30 seconds**. That matches the delay users describe. Common culprits:

- A corporate proxy or secure web gateway that doesn't support WebSocket upgrades, or that inspects TLS traffic.
- A firewall that closes idle connections after a short time.
- Browser extensions (privacy or ad-blocking tools).

## Confirm

1. In the app, open **Help > Connection diagnostics**.

article_number: KA-0019
title: Setting up webhooks and fixing delivery failures
url_name: webhooks-setup-troubleshooting
article_type: Troubleshooting
category: API & Integrations
plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-09-14
related_cases: [CASE-1004]
summary: How webhook registration, verification, signatures and retries work, and how to diagnose 500 errors and failed deliveries.
---

## How webhooks work

1. Register an endpoint: **Settings > API > Webhooks > Add endpoint**, or `POST /v2/webhooks`.
2. Lumora sends a **verification request** with `{"type":"verification","challenge":"..."}`. Your endpoint must reply `200` within 10 seconds with the `challenge` value in the body.
3. Each event is a `POST` with a JSON body. It is signed in the `X-Lumora-Signature` header (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body using the endpoint secret).
4. If your endpoint returns anything other than 2xx, or takes longer than 10 seconds, Lumora retries 5 times over 24 hours with exponential backoff. After 24 hours of failures, the endpoint is **disabled**.

## "500 errors when setting up webhooks"

- A firewall that closes idle connections after a short time.
- Browser extensions (privacy or ad-blocking tools).

## Confirm

1. In the app, open **Help > Connection diagnostics**. It shows **Live updates: Connected (WebSocket)** or **Fallback (polling)**.
2. Or, in the browser DevTools **Network** tab, filter by **WS** and look for a connection to `rt.lumora.example`.

## Fix

Send this to the customer's IT team:

- Allow WebSocket (HTTP Upgrade) traffic to `rt.lumora.example` on port 443.
- Exclude `*.lumora.example` from TLS inspection.
- Set the idle timeout for these connections to at least 120 seconds. The app sends a heartbeat every 45 seconds.

## If WebSockets are connected and it's still slow

Collect the diagnostics output and a HAR file, and escalate to the Realtime team with the workspace ID and the object that was being edited.

To recover events missed while your webhook endpoint was disabled, follow these steps:

1. **Fix the underlying issue first.** Your endpoint was disabled because it returned non-2xx responses (or took longer than 10 seconds) for 5 retry attempts over a 24-hour period of exponential backoff — once that window elapsed with continued failures, Lumora disabled the endpoint.
2. **Re-enable the endpoint.** Go to the endpoint page and click **Re-enable**.

Only events from the **last 72 hours** can be replayed this way. If the outage caused failures further back than that, those events cannot be recovered through this replay mechanism, based on the available documentation.

- Your code doesn't handle the verification `challenge` request correctly.
- Your signature check is validating against *parsed and re-serialized* JSON instead of the **raw request body**.
- Your handler does slow processing before responding — best practice is to respond `200` immediately and process the event asynchronously in the background.

Once you've confirmed the endpoint is fixed (e.g., via **Send test event**), click **Re-enable** and select **Replay failed events** to get the last 72 hours of missed events resent.

## Priority

**Settings > Security > Audit log > Streaming** supports Splunk HEC, Datadog, Amazon S3, and a generic HTTPS endpoint. Events arrive within 60 seconds.

## Compliance documents

Customers can download SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 reports, plus the DPA, from the Trust Center at `trust.lumora.example` after signing an NDA. Don't attach these documents to cases.

## Support channels

| Plan | Channels | Hours |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | Help center, community forum, email | Business hours, best effort |
| Team | Email, web form | Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00 ET |
| Business | Email, web form, chat | 24×5 |
| Enterprise | All above plus phone and named CSM | 24×7 for Urgent |

## Priority definitions

- **Urgent**: Production is down or unusable for most users, or payments/data integrity are affected, with no workaround. Examples: the mobile app crashes on launch for all users, the payment gateway is failing, invitation emails stop going out to everyone.
- **High**: A major feature is broken or badly degraded and the workaround is painful. Examples: webhooks returning 500, exports coming out empty, sensitive data appearing in exports.

- **Urgent**: Production is down or unusable for most users, or payments/data integrity are affected, with no workaround. Examples: the mobile app crashes on launch for all users, the payment gateway is failing, invitation emails stop going out to everyone.

- **Low**: General questions, feature requests, cosmetic issues.

article_type: Troubleshooting
category: API & Integrations
plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-10-07
related_cases: [CASE-1014]
summary: How to diagnose data connectors that take 30+ minutes to sync instead of the usual interval (source throttling, full resyncs, errors, plan interval).
---

## Expected interval

Incremental syncs run every **15 minutes on Team** and **5 minutes on Business and Enterprise** (KA-0001). A sync normally takes under a minute for a few thousand changed records.

## Diagnose

Open **Settings > Integrations > [connector] > Sync log**. For each run it shows the start time, duration, records processed, and any warnings.

| What the sync log shows | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `Throttled by source (429)` | The *external system* is limiting Lumora's requests | Raise the API limit in the source system, or reduce the fields being synced |
| `Full resync in progress` | A schema change or a re-authorization started a full resync | Wait. Incremental syncs resume afterwards. Large sources can take hours |

3. Click **Verify**. DNS changes can take up to 24 hours to spread, but usually take minutes.
4. Lumora issues and renews the TLS certificate automatically. If your domain has **CAA** records, add `letsencrypt.org`.
5. When the status shows **Active**, the old `lumora.example` address redirects to the custom domain.

## After switching

- Update the SSO settings in your IdP: the Entity ID and ACS URL change to the custom domain (KA-0007). Lumora accepts both the old and new addresses for 14 days.
- Webhook and API URLs **don't change**. The API stays on `api.lumora.example`.
- Links in existing emails and bookmarks keep working through the redirect.

## Troubleshooting

| Status | Fix |
|---|---|
| `CNAME not found` | Check the record. Some DNS providers add the zone name automatically |
| `Certificate pending` for more than 1 hour | Check CAA records. Make sure there's no proxy (orange-cloud style) in front of the CNAME |

| `Throttled by source (429)` | The *external system* is limiting Lumora's requests | Raise the API limit in the source system, or reduce the fields being synced |
| `Full resync in progress` | A schema change or a re-authorization started a full resync | Wait. Incremental syncs resume afterwards. Large sources can take hours |
| Runs are skipped or overlap | The previous sync hadn't finished when the next was due | Reduce the objects or fields synced, or ask for a longer interval |
| `Auth error` | The connection's credentials expired | Reconnect (see KA-0031 for Salesforce) |
| Nothing unusual, but runs are long | Possibly a backlog on Lumora's side | Check the status page, then escalate |

## Reduce sync volume

- Under **Connector > Objects**, turn off objects you don't use.
- Under **Connector > Filters**, sync only active records, for example `Status != Closed`.
- Avoid formula or rollup fields in the source system that change on every record each night. They make every record look modified.

## Escalate

Include the connector type, the workspace ID, and a screenshot or export of the sync log covering the slow period.

title: Setting up webhooks and fixing delivery failures
url_name: webhooks-setup-troubleshooting
article_type: Troubleshooting
category: API & Integrations
plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-09-14
related_cases: [CASE-1004]
summary: How webhook registration, verification, signatures and retries work, and how to diagnose 500 errors and failed deliveries.
---

## How webhooks work

1. Register an endpoint: **Settings > API > Webhooks > Add endpoint**, or `POST /v2/webhooks`.
2. Lumora sends a **verification request** with `{"type":"verification","challenge":"..."}`. Your endpoint must reply `200` within 10 seconds with the `challenge` value in the body.
3. Each event is a `POST` with a JSON body. It is signed in the `X-Lumora-Signature` header (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body using the endpoint secret).
4. If your endpoint returns anything other than 2xx, or takes longer than 10 seconds, Lumora retries 5 times over 24 hours with exponential backoff. After 24 hours of failures, the endpoint is **disabled**.

## "500 errors when setting up webhooks"

3. Change **Reset link lifetime**, **Failed attempts before lockout**, and **Lockout duration**.
4. Click **Save**. The new settings apply to the next sign-in attempt or reset request. Links that were already sent keep their original lifetime.

## "I was locked out for 24 hours after only 3 tries"

That's not a bug. It means the workspace admin has set a strict policy (3 attempts, 24-hour lockout). Explain that their own admin controls this setting. The admin can unlock the account right away (see below).

## Unlock a user

**Settings > Members**, select the user, then **⋯ > Unlock account**. The user can sign in immediately. Support agents can also unlock a user from the Support Console after confirming the request with a workspace Admin.

## Security guidance

For reset links longer than 4 hours, we recommend turning on 2FA (KA-0006) so a forwarded or intercepted link can't be used on its own.

Q19.answer:
This is a known behavior described in Lumora's troubleshooting guide for empty or incomplete CSV exports (KA-0021).

## Why this happens

Your table has 120,000 rows, which is **over the 50,000-row threshold** for immediate downloads. Exports above that size are meant to run in the background, but if you triggered the export from an older bookmarked link or an outdated UI state, it can still attempt an immediate download — which returns an empty file instead.

## How to fix it

1. **Use the background export option.** Instead of a direct download, choose **Export > CSV (email me when ready)**. You'll receive a download link by email, valid for **7 days**. The maximum export size is **1,000,000 rows**, so your 120,000-row table is well within range.
2. **Double-check filters.** If the on-screen view has a temporary filter not applied to the export (or vice versa), rows can be missing. Save the view first (**Save view**) and then export from that saved view to keep the results consistent.
3. **Check field-level permissions.** If columns in the export are restricted by your project role, they're excluded — and if *every* selected column is restricted, the resulting file will be completely empty. Verify your project role under **Settings**.
4. **Check for Sensitive fields.** Any field marked *Sensitive* is stripped from exports unless you have the **Export sensitive data** permission.
5. **Rule out an Excel display issue.** If the file isn't actually empty but just *looks* blank when opened by double-clicking in Excel, use **Data > From Text/CSV** in Excel, or export using **CSV (Excel compatible)**, which adds a byte-order mark for proper encoding detection.

## If it's still empty

If none of the above resolves it, escalate to Reports Engineering with the following details:
- The report URL
- The exact time of the export attempt
- The browser used
- A HAR file capturing the export request

Start with option 1 (the background/email export) since 120,000 rows exceeds the immediate-download limit — that's the most likely cause here.

article_number: KA-0028
title: Browser lags when filtering tables with 100,000+ rows
url_name: filtering-large-tables
article_type: Troubleshooting
category: Performance
plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-10-03
related_cases: [CASE-1039]
summary: How to keep very large tables responsive with server-side filtering, saved views, indexed fields and paging.
---

## Symptoms

Filtering or sorting a table view with more than about 100,000 rows makes the browser freeze for several seconds, or shows "Page unresponsive".

## Why it happens

By default, table views load up to 100,000 rows into the browser so that quick filters respond immediately. Above that size, filtering in the browser uses a lot of memory and CPU, especially with formula columns.

## Resolution

1. **Turn on server-side filtering.** In the view, go to **View settings > Performance > Filter on server**. Filters and sorts then run on Lumora's servers and only one page of results (500 rows) is loaded. This is the main fix.
2. **Filter on indexed fields.** Status, Assignee, Created date, Due date, Project and any custom field with **Indexed** ticked (**Settings > Fields > Edit**) filter much faster.

Choose **Change role**, **Change seat**, **Deactivate** or **Remove**.

## CSV import

1. Go to **Settings > Members > Import > Download template**.
2. Fill in the columns `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `role` (`admin`, `member` or `guest`), `seat` (`full` or `viewer`), `action` (`add`, `update`, `deactivate` or `remove`) and an optional `projects` column, separated by semicolons.
3. Upload the file. Lumora shows a preview with row-level errors before anything changes.
4. Confirm. You can import up to 5,000 rows per file. Invitations go out as each row is processed.

## Deactivate or remove?

- **Deactivate** frees the seat and keeps everything the user created assigned to them. You can reverse it.
- **Remove** frees the seat and moves their open tasks to the person you choose. You can't reverse it.

## SCIM

On Enterprise, generate a token under **Settings > Security > SCIM** and enter it with the base URL `https://api.lumora.example/scim/v2` in your IdP. Users and group-to-role mappings then come from the IdP.

Filters and sorts then run on Lumora's servers and only one page of results (500 rows) is loaded. This is the main fix.
2. **Filter on indexed fields.** Status, Assignee, Created date, Due date, Project and any custom field with **Indexed** ticked (**Settings > Fields > Edit**) filter much faster. Business includes up to 20 indexed custom fields, Enterprise up to 100.
3. **Use saved views** with the filters already set, so the full table never loads.
4. **Hide formula columns** you don't need in that view.
5. **Archive old rows.** Moving completed items older than 12 months to an archive table can make the main table much smaller.

## Notes

- From release 2026.11, server-side filtering turns on automatically above 50,000 rows.
- If the problem continues with server-side filtering on, collect a HAR file and a browser performance profile and escalate to Frontend Engineering.

- **High**: A major feature is broken or badly degraded and the workaround is painful. Examples: webhooks returning 500, exports coming out empty, sensitive data appearing in exports.

## Before you escalate

## Requesting a restore from backup

For anything not covered above (for example a project bulk-edited by mistake, or data deleted more than 30 days ago but still within the backup window):

3. Restores are done **into a new copy of the project**, never over live data. The customer then copies back what they need.
4. Target time: 2 business days (Enterprise: 1 business day). There is no charge on Business and Enterprise. On Starter and Team, the first restore each year is free.

Q22.answer:
This matches a known defect affecting scheduled reports created before a certain release.

## Why this happens
Schedules created **before release 2026.08.2** had a bug where the timezone was saved internally as **UTC**, no matter what timezone was actually selected (e.g., *America/New_York*). Since your schedule was set up back in July — before that fix shipped — it would show "New York" in its settings but actually run on UTC time, which explains why it's firing at the wrong hour.

Note that this is *not* a daylight-saving issue: schedules follow local time for their timezone, so a 09:00 New York schedule stays at 09:00 even after clocks change. The wrong-hour symptom you're seeing is specifically the pre-2026.08.2 UTC-save defect.

## How to fix it
1. Open the schedule and confirm its **Timezone** field (it will likely still show *America/New_York*, but is actually running in UTC).
2. Edit the schedule: change any setting, then change it back.
3. Click **Save** — this rewrites the stored timezone correctly, after which it will run at the intended New York hour.

No need to recreate the schedule from scratch; the edit-and-resave step resolves it for any schedule created before the 2026.08.2 fix.

## Symptoms

A report over a long date range (for example 6 months of task data) takes 5 to 15 minutes, or times out.

## Why it happens

Detail reports read every row in the range and work out calculated fields for each one when the report runs. These are the main costs:

- **Calculated and formula columns**, especially ones that look up data in other projects.
- **Grouping by a text field** that has many different values.
- **Including archived projects**.
- **"Status history" fields**, which read the full change log.

## Speed it up

1. **Turn on summary mode.** In the report, go to **Settings > Data source > Use daily summaries**. Summary mode reads pre-calculated daily totals. A 6-month report usually finishes in under 30 seconds. You lose row-level detail, but you can still drill into a single day.

Q23.answer:
This is a known issue covered in our knowledge base article on stale dashboard widgets. Here are the likely causes, in order of how common they are, with fixes:

## Why one widget is stuck on July data

- **Fixed date range (most common cause).** The widget's filter may be set to an absolute date range (e.g., *1 Jul – 31 Jul*) instead of a relative one. **Fix:** Edit the widget → **Filters > Date** → change it to a relative option like **This month** or **Last 30 days**.
- **Source report is a paused snapshot.** If the widget pulls from a report using **Save as snapshot**, it will keep showing the last snapshot taken. Snapshots pause automatically if the report owner's account is deactivated. **Fix:** Open the source report and check **Last refreshed**; if it's paused, assign a new owner or switch the report to live data.
- **Data connector stopped syncing.** If the revenue figure comes from an external billing system via a connector, the sync may have failed. **Fix:** Check **Settings > Integrations > [connector] > Sync log** for errors.
- **Cache.** Widgets cache for up to 15 minutes. **Fix:** Click **⋯ > Refresh** on the widget — but if it's still showing July data after refreshing, caching isn't the real cause.
- **Wrong source report after duplicating a dashboard.** If this dashboard was copied from another one, the widget may still be pointing at the *original* report instead of the new one. **Fix:** Check **Edit widget > Source** to confirm it points to the right report.

## If none of these fix it

Escalate to Reports Engineering with the dashboard URL, the widget's name, the value you expected to see, and the value currently shown.

Would you like help walking through any of these steps, for example checking the widget's filter settings or the connector sync log?

summary: Changes from other users showing up about 30 seconds late almost always means WebSockets are blocked and the app has fallen back to polling. Here is how to confirm and fix it.
---

## Symptoms

When several people edit the same board, document or task at once, each person's changes reach the others about **30 seconds** late instead of immediately. Users may also see edit conflicts.

## Cause

Lumora sends live updates over a WebSocket connection to `wss://rt.lumora.example`. If something on the network blocks or breaks WebSockets, the app quietly falls back to **polling every 30 seconds**. That matches the delay users describe. Common culprits:

- A corporate proxy or secure web gateway that doesn't support WebSocket upgrades, or that inspects TLS traffic.
- A firewall that closes idle connections after a short time.
- Browser extensions (privacy or ad-blocking tools).

## Confirm

1. In the app, open **Help > Connection diagnostics**.

Each attempt shows the gateway's response code.

| Error in log | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `authentication_failed` / `invalid_api_key` | The API key was rotated or revoked in the gateway dashboard | Reconnect the gateway: **Settings > Integrations > Payments > Reconnect** |
| `webhook_signature_invalid` | The webhook signing secret changed | Copy the new secret into Lumora's payment settings |
| `currency_not_supported` | The form's currency changed to one the merchant account doesn't support | Change the form currency back, or enable the currency in the gateway |
| `account_restricted` | The gateway has restricted the merchant account (verification, compliance) | The customer must resolve it with their payment provider |
| `test_mode_key_in_live` | A test key was entered on a live form | Use the live key |
| No entries at all | The form doesn't reach the payment step | Check the payment field's conditional logic |

## Step 3: Tell the customer

- Payments are processed by the customer's own payment provider. Lumora doesn't hold card data.
- Failed submissions are saved as **Unpaid**. After the fix, the customer can send each submitter a payment link from **Responses > Unpaid > Send payment link**.

Q24.answer:
This is a known performance issue with very large tables in Lumora. With 200,000 rows you're well above the default 100,000-row browser-side load limit, so filtering/sorting becomes slow and can freeze the tab.

## Why it happens
By default, table views load up to 100,000 rows directly into the browser so quick filters feel instant. Beyond that, in-browser filtering consumes a lot of memory and CPU — especially if the view has formula columns — which is why a 200,000-row table struggles.

## How to fix it
- **Turn on server-side filtering** (the main fix): go to **View settings > Performance > Filter on server**. Filters and sorts then run on Lumora's servers, and only one page of results (500 rows) loads into the browser at a time.
- **Filter on indexed fields.** Status, Assignee, Created date, Due date, Project, and any custom field with **Indexed** ticked (**Settings > Fields > Edit**) filter much faster. Business plans get up to 20 indexed custom fields, Enterprise up to 100.
- **Use saved views** with filters already applied, so the full table never has to load.
- **Hide formula columns** you don't need in that particular view.
- **Archive old rows** — moving completed items older than 12 months to an archive table can shrink the main table significantly.

## Good to know
Starting with release **2026.11**, server-side filtering will turn on automatically for any table above 50,000 rows, so this should become less of an issue going forward.

If you turn on server-side filtering and the freezing continues, the next step is to collect a HAR file and a browser performance profile so it can be escalated to Frontend Engineering. Let me know if you'd like help capturing that HAR file or walking through the server-side filtering setting.

## How webhooks work

1. Register an endpoint: **Settings > API > Webhooks > Add endpoint**, or `POST /v2/webhooks`.
2. Lumora sends a **verification request** with `{"type":"verification","challenge":"..."}`. Your endpoint must reply `200` within 10 seconds with the `challenge` value in the body.
3. Each event is a `POST` with a JSON body. It is signed in the `X-Lumora-Signature` header (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body using the endpoint secret).
4. If your endpoint returns anything other than 2xx, or takes longer than 10 seconds, Lumora retries 5 times over 24 hours with exponential backoff. After 24 hours of failures, the endpoint is **disabled**.

## "500 errors when setting up webhooks"

## Step 3: Customer-side checks

1. Open `https://lumora.example/speedtest`, which measures latency to the nearest Lumora region.
2. Try a private browser window with extensions turned off. Ad blockers and some security extensions slow down the app considerably.
3. Make sure the corporate proxy allows WebSockets to `rt.lumora.example`. Without them the app falls back to slower polling (KA-0029).
4. Check the browser is supported and the device has at least 8 GB of RAM if it opens boards with thousands of cards.

## Step 4: Workspace-side checks (agent)

In the Support Console, open **Workspace > Health**:

- **Automation runs per hour.** Bulk automations scheduled at a fixed time can slow down that workspace. Suggest spreading them out.
- **Connector syncs.** Large full syncs can be moved to off-peak hours.

## Step 5: Escalate with data

Include the workspace ID, the affected users, time windows **with timezone**, speed test results, and a HAR file captured while the app was slow (KA-0003).

4. If your endpoint returns anything other than 2xx, or takes longer than 10 seconds, Lumora retries 5 times over 24 hours with exponential backoff. After 24 hours of failures, the endpoint is **disabled**.

## "500 errors when setting up webhooks"

First work out **who** is returning the 500:

- **The customer's endpoint returns 500** (shown in **Webhooks > Endpoint > Delivery log**). The problem is in their code. Common causes:
  - The verification `challenge` isn't handled, so their code fails trying to parse an event it doesn't expect.
  - The signature is checked against *parsed and re-serialized* JSON instead of the raw request body.
  - The handler does slow work before responding. Respond `200` first and process the event in the background.
- **The Lumora API returns 500 to `POST /v2/webhooks`.** Usually the URL is invalid, isn't HTTPS, or points to a private IP address, and the API returns a 500 where it should return a 400. That is known defect ENG-4210. Check that the URL is public HTTPS with a valid certificate. If it still fails, escalate with the `X-Request-Id` from the response.

## Re-enable a disabled endpoint

Fix the endpoint, then click **Re-enable**.

- A firewall that closes idle connections after a short time.
- Browser extensions (privacy or ad-blocking tools).

## Confirm

1. In the app, open **Help > Connection diagnostics**. It shows **Live updates: Connected (WebSocket)** or **Fallback (polling)**.
2. Or, in the browser DevTools **Network** tab, filter by **WS** and look for a connection to `rt.lumora.example`.

## Fix

Send this to the customer's IT team:

- Allow WebSocket (HTTP Upgrade) traffic to `rt.lumora.example` on port 443.
- Exclude `*.lumora.example` from TLS inspection.
- Set the idle timeout for these connections to at least 120 seconds. The app sends a heartbeat every 45 seconds.

Collect the diagnostics output and a HAR file, and escalate to the Realtime team with the workspace ID and the object that was being edited.

The latest two major versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. Internet Explorer and legacy Edge are not supported.

Q25.answer:
A disconnect that happens on a precise, regular schedule (like every 12 hours) is the classic signature of the **Refresh Token Policy** setting in Salesforce — this is the most common cause of recurring Salesforce connector disconnects in Lumora.

## What's happening

In Salesforce, the Connected App for Lumora Workspace has a **Refresh Token Policy**. If it's configured to "Expire refresh token after X hours" instead of "Refresh token is valid until revoked," Salesforce will force the connector to disconnect on that exact schedule — in your case, every 12 hours.

## How to fix it

1. In Salesforce, go to **Setup > Connected Apps OAuth Usage > Lumora Workspace > Manage > Edit Policies**.
2. Find **Refresh Token Policy** and change it to **"Refresh token is valid until revoked"**.
3. Save the change — this should stop the recurring disconnects going forward.

## Other things to rule out if the above doesn't fully resolve it

- **Connecting user issues**: The connector runs as whichever Salesforce user authorized it. If that user's password changes or they get deactivated, the connection breaks — use a dedicated **integration user** whose password never expires.
- **IP restrictions**: If Salesforce's **Permitted Users** setting requires pre-authorization or IP relaxation is set to enforce restrictions, you'll need to allowlist Lumora's outbound IPs (listed at `https://lumora.example/ips`) on the integration user's profile, or relax IP restrictions for the Lumora connected app.
- **API limits**: If the org hits its daily Salesforce API limit, calls get rejected and Lumora shows this as a disconnect — check **Setup > Company Information > API Requests, Last 24 Hours**.
- **Sandbox refresh**: Refreshing a Salesforce sandbox wipes all OAuth grants, requiring reconnection.
- **Too many tokens**: Salesforce allows only 5 refresh tokens per user per connected app — authorizing more silently revokes the oldest one, so avoid sharing one integration user across multiple Lumora workspaces.

## To reconnect

Go to **Settings > Integrations > Salesforce > Reconnect**, signed in as the integration user — your field mappings will be preserved.

Given the exact 12-hour regularity you're describing, I'd check the Refresh Token Policy first, as that's by far the most likely culprit for a clockwork-timed disconnect.

## Symptoms

The Salesforce connector shows **Disconnected — reauthorization required** every few hours or days. Syncs stop until someone reconnects it.

## Causes and resolution

1. **Refresh token policy in Salesforce.** In Salesforce Setup, go to **Connected Apps OAuth Usage > Lumora Workspace > Manage > Edit Policies**. Set **Refresh Token Policy** to *Refresh token is valid until revoked*. If it's set to "Expire refresh token after X hours", the connector disconnects on that schedule. This is the most common cause.
2. **The connecting user's password changed or they were deactivated.** The connector runs as the Salesforce user who authorized it. Use a dedicated **integration user** whose password never expires.
3.

2. **The connecting user's password changed or they were deactivated.** The connector runs as the Salesforce user who authorized it. Use a dedicated **integration user** whose password never expires.
3. **IP restrictions.** If **Permitted Users** is set to *Admin approved users are pre-authorized* or IP relaxation is set to *Enforce IP restrictions*, allow Lumora's outbound IPs (listed at `https://lumora.example/ips`) on the integration user's profile, or set **IP Relaxation** to *Relax IP restrictions* for the Lumora connected app.
4. **Salesforce API limit reached.** When the org hits its daily API limit, Salesforce rejects the calls. Lumora shows this as a disconnect. Check **Setup > Company Information > API Requests, Last 24 Hours**.
5. **Sandbox refresh.** Refreshing a sandbox removes all OAuth grants. Reconnect afterwards.
6. **Too many tokens.** Salesforce allows 5 refresh tokens per user per connected app. Authorizing more than that silently revokes the oldest one. Don't share one integration user across several Lumora workspaces.

## Reconnect

**Settings > Integrations > Salesforce > Reconnect**, signed in as the integration user. Field mappings are kept.

| `Throttled by source (429)` | The *external system* is limiting Lumora's requests | Raise the API limit in the source system, or reduce the fields being synced |
| `Full resync in progress` | A schema change or a re-authorization started a full resync | Wait. Incremental syncs resume afterwards. Large sources can take hours |
| Runs are skipped or overlap | The previous sync hadn't finished when the next was due | Reduce the objects or fields synced, or ask for a longer interval |
| `Auth error` | The connection's credentials expired | Reconnect (see KA-0031 for Salesforce) |
| Nothing unusual, but runs are long | Possibly a backlog on Lumora's side | Check the status page, then escalate |

## Reduce sync volume

- Under **Connector > Objects**, turn off objects you don't use.
- Under **Connector > Filters**, sync only active records, for example `Status != Closed`.
- Avoid formula or rollup fields in the source system that change on every record each night. They make every record look modified.

## Escalate

Include the connector type, the workspace ID, and a screenshot or export of the sync log covering the slow period.

## Status

**Open.** Engineering ticket ENG-4471. Fix planned for release **2026.11.1**.

## Symptoms

- A user logs out through their identity provider portal (IdP-initiated logout), but Lumora tabs that are already open keep working.
- After logout, pressing Back or reopening the app shows cached project data until the page is refreshed.

## Cause

There are two separate problems:

1. If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL**, Lumora never hears about the IdP logout. The Lumora session lasts until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
2. Even when Single Logout is set up, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout.

1. If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL**, Lumora never hears about the IdP logout. The Lumora session lasts until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
2. Even when Single Logout is set up, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout. This is the defect being fixed in 2026.11.1.

## Workarounds

1. Make sure Single Logout is configured in **both** the IdP and in Lumora (**Settings > Security > Single sign-on > Edit > Single Logout URL**). This ends the server-side session.
2. Shorten **Settings > Security > Session lifetime** to as little as 1 hour.
3. On shared or kiosk devices, turn on **Settings > Security > Disable offline cache**. Users lose offline access, but nothing is cached on the device.
4. Users can sign out with **Profile > Sign out** in Lumora as well as in the IdP. That clears the local cache.

## Customer messaging

Tell customers that server-side sessions **are** ended when Single Logout is configured. The remaining risk is data cached in the browser on that device. Link the case to ENG-4471 so the customer is notified when the fix ships.

Limits apply **per workspace per minute**, shared by **every** API token and installed integration in that workspace. This is the most common reason a customer says "we're hitting the limit even though we're within it": their own integration is sharing the allowance with other apps, such as the Salesforce connector, Zapier-style tools or a BI connector.

| Business | 300 | 50 |
| Enterprise | 1,000 | 200 |

Search endpoints (`/v2/search`) have a separate limit of 30 per minute on every plan.

## Response headers

Every response includes:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: the workspace's allowance
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: requests left in the current window

If the **Transaction log** (found at **Settings > Payments > Transaction log** on the form) has no entries at all, it means the form never reaches the payment step in the first place. In other words, the payment gateway isn't even being attempted/called — the submission flow is stopping before it gets to the payment field.

The recommended fix is to check the payment field's **conditional logic** on the form, since misconfigured conditions can prevent respondents from ever reaching the payment step.

This is different from the other logged errors (like `authentication_failed`, `webhook_signature_invalid`, `currency_not_supported`, etc.), which indicate the form *did* reach the payment step but the gateway rejected or failed the attempt. Since failed/incomplete payments mean lost revenue for the customer, this type of issue should be treated as **Urgent**.

## Firefox

1. Press **F12** and open **Network**. Tick **Persist Logs**.
2. Reproduce the problem.

## Safari

2. Choose **Develop > Show Web Inspector > Network**, tick **Preserve Log**, and reproduce.
3. Click **Export**.

## Privacy

HAR files can contain session cookies. Ask customers to upload them through the secure attachment link on the case, never by email. Support deletes attachments 30 days after the case closes.

Q27.answer:
This is a known behavior, not a bug on Lumora's end (though there's a related UI glitch) — a custom field can't be deleted while anything is still using it. 

## Why this happens

A field is blocked from deletion if it's referenced by any of the following:
- Automation rule conditions or actions
- Report filters, columns, groupings, or dashboard widgets
- Form questions mapped to the field
- Formula fields that refer to it
- Integration field mappings (e.g., the Salesforce connector)
- Required-field rules on a project 

**Note on the "nothing happens" symptom:** There's a known UI defect (ENG-4502) where the message listing these references closes immediately, making it look like clicking Delete did nothing at all. A fix is due in release 2026.11.1.

## How to fix it

1. Go to **Settings > Fields**, open the field, and click the **Usage** tab — it lists every place the field is referenced, with a link to each.
2. Remove or change each reference: edit the automation, report, or form, or remap the integration field.
3. Go back to the field and click **Delete** again.

## Alternative: Archive instead of delete

If the field is used in many places and removing all references isn't practical, you can click **Archive field** instead. This hides it from forms, views, and pickers while keeping past values and references intact — and it can be restored at any time.

## If you still delete it

Deleted custom fields (and their values) can be restored for 30 days via **Settings > Fields > Deleted**.

title: Browser lags when filtering tables with 100,000+ rows
url_name: filtering-large-tables
article_type: Troubleshooting
category: Performance
plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-10-03
related_cases: [CASE-1039]
summary: How to keep very large tables responsive with server-side filtering, saved views, indexed fields and paging.
---

## Symptoms

Filtering or sorting a table view with more than about 100,000 rows makes the browser freeze for several seconds, or shows "Page unresponsive".

## Why it happens

By default, table views load up to 100,000 rows into the browser so that quick filters respond immediately. Above that size, filtering in the browser uses a lot of memory and CPU, especially with formula columns.

## Resolution

1. **Turn on server-side filtering.** In the view, go to **View settings > Performance > Filter on server**. Filters and sorts then run on Lumora's servers and only one page of results (500 rows) is loaded. This is the main fix.
2. **Filter on indexed fields.** Status, Assignee, Created date, Due date, Project and any custom field with **Indexed** ticked (**Settings > Fields > Edit**) filter much faster.

Filters and sorts then run on Lumora's servers and only one page of results (500 rows) is loaded. This is the main fix.
2. **Filter on indexed fields.** Status, Assignee, Created date, Due date, Project and any custom field with **Indexed** ticked (**Settings > Fields > Edit**) filter much faster. Business includes up to 20 indexed custom fields, Enterprise up to 100.
3. **Use saved views** with the filters already set, so the full table never loads.
4. **Hide formula columns** you don't need in that view.
5. **Archive old rows.** Moving completed items older than 12 months to an archive table can make the main table much smaller.

## Notes

- From release 2026.11, server-side filtering turns on automatically above 50,000 rows.
- If the problem continues with server-side filtering on, collect a HAR file and a browser performance profile and escalate to Frontend Engineering.

Q28.answer: A scheduled rule that updates 200 tasks counts as **200 runs** — one run per task it updates. This is because a run is counted per task affected, not per rule trigger, for scheduled rules that act on multiple items.
chunk_texts:
## What counts as a run?

One run is one rule triggering once, however many actions it carries out. Some examples:

- A rule that runs when a task's status changes, and posts a comment and sends an email, counts as **1 run**.
- A scheduled rule that updates 200 tasks counts as **200 runs** (one per task).
- Runs where the conditions aren't met **don't** count.

## What happens at the limit?

- **Active rules:** You can't activate another rule until one is paused.
- **Monthly runs:** Owners get an email at 80% and 100%. At 100%, rules stop running until the next billing month. Paid plans can buy run packs (+25,000) under **Settings > Billing > Add-ons**.

## Other limits

- Rules can call each other up to 10 levels deep. After that, the chain is stopped to prevent loops.
- Each scheduled rule can process up to 5,000 items per run.
- See usage under **Settings > Automations > Usage**.

## Response headers

Every response includes:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: the workspace's allowance
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: requests left in the current window
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: when the window resets, as Unix epoch seconds

When the limit is exceeded, the API returns **429 Too Many Requests** with a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

## Best practices

1. Honor `Retry-After`, and use exponential backoff with jitter.
2. Use **webhooks** instead of polling for changes (KA-0019).
3. Use batch endpoints (`POST /v2/tasks/batch`, up to 100 items).
4. Request only the fields you need with `?fields=`.

## Investigating a complaint

**Settings > API > Usage** shows requests per token and per integration for the last 7 days. Ask the customer for a screenshot. Usually one integration is using most of the allowance. Enterprise customers can buy a higher limit through their CSM.

## Symptoms

A report over a long date range (for example 6 months of task data) takes 5 to 15 minutes, or times out.

## Why it happens

Detail reports read every row in the range and work out calculated fields for each one when the report runs. These are the main costs:

- **Calculated and formula columns**, especially ones that look up data in other projects.
- **Grouping by a text field** that has many different values.
- **Including archived projects**.
- **"Status history" fields**, which read the full change log.

## Speed it up

1. **Turn on summary mode.** In the report, go to **Settings > Data source > Use daily summaries**. Summary mode reads pre-calculated daily totals. A 6-month report usually finishes in under 30 seconds. You lose row-level detail, but you can still drill into a single day.

Q29.answer:
This is expected behavior if your task's recurrence is set to **"Daily"** — that setting includes weekends by design.

## How to fix it

- **Skip weekends:** Open the task and go to **Repeat**, then choose **Every weekday (Mon–Fri)** instead of **Daily**.
- **Non-standard work week** (e.g., Sunday–Thursday): An Admin can set this under **Settings > Workspace > Working days**, then choose **Repeat > Every working day** on the task.
- **Also skip public holidays:** Add a holiday calendar under **Settings > Workspace > Holidays**, and tick **Skip holidays** on the recurrence.

## A known defect to check for

If your recurrence is already set to **Every weekday** but a weekend task still slipped through, this may be related to a now-fixed defect: recurrences created *before* a daylight saving time change could generate one extra task on the weekend, because the next date was calculated in UTC. This was fixed in version **2026.09.3**. If you're on a version at or after that fix and still see this, simply **open the affected recurrence and click Save again** — this forces the schedule to recalculate correctly.

## Cleaning up tasks already created by mistake

To remove any weekend tasks that were created in error:
1. Filter the project by **Created by: Recurrence** and **Due date: is weekend**.
2. Select the unwanted tasks and delete them.

Note that deleting these individual occurrences will not affect the rest of the recurring series.

title: Real-time collaboration changes appear with a delay

category: Performance

last_reviewed: 2026-09-26
related_cases: [CASE-1032]
summary: Changes from other users showing up about 30 seconds late almost always means WebSockets are blocked and the app has fallen back to polling. Here is how to confirm and fix it.
---

## Symptoms

When several people edit the same board, document or task at once, each person's changes reach the others about **30 seconds** late instead of immediately. Users may also see edit conflicts.

## Cause

Lumora sends live updates over a WebSocket connection to `wss://rt.lumora.example`. If something on the network blocks or breaks WebSockets, the app quietly falls back to **polling every 30 seconds**. That matches the delay users describe. Common culprits:

- A corporate proxy or secure web gateway that doesn't support WebSocket upgrades, or that inspects TLS traffic.
- A firewall that closes idle connections after a short time.
- Browser extensions (privacy or ad-blocking tools).

## Confirm

article_number: KA-0029
title: Real-time collaboration changes appear with a delay
url_name: realtime-collaboration-delay
article_type: Troubleshooting
category: Performance
plans: [Starter, Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-09-26
related_cases: [CASE-1032]
summary: Changes from other users showing up about 30 seconds late almost always means WebSockets are blocked and the app has fallen back to polling. Here is how to confirm and fix it.
---

## Symptoms

When several people edit the same board, document or task at once, each person's changes reach the others about **30 seconds** late instead of immediately. Users may also see edit conflicts.

## Cause

Lumora sends live updates over a WebSocket connection to `wss://rt.lumora.example`. If something on the network blocks or breaks WebSockets, the app quietly falls back to **polling every 30 seconds**. That matches the delay users describe. Common culprits:

- A corporate proxy or secure web gateway that doesn't support WebSocket upgrades, or that inspects TLS traffic.
- A firewall that closes idle connections after a short time.
- Browser extensions (privacy or ad-blocking tools).

## Confirm

1. In the app, open **Help > Connection diagnostics**.

1. If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL**, Lumora never hears about the IdP logout. The Lumora session lasts until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
2. Even when Single Logout is set up, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout. This is the defect being fixed in 2026.11.1.

## Workarounds

1. Make sure Single Logout is configured in **both** the IdP and in Lumora (**Settings > Security > Single sign-on > Edit > Single Logout URL**). This ends the server-side session.
2. Shorten **Settings > Security > Session lifetime** to as little as 1 hour.
3. On shared or kiosk devices, turn on **Settings > Security > Disable offline cache**. Users lose offline access, but nothing is cached on the device.
4. Users can sign out with **Profile > Sign out** in Lumora as well as in the IdP. That clears the local cache.

## Customer messaging

Tell customers that server-side sessions **are** ended when Single Logout is configured. The remaining risk is data cached in the browser on that device. Link the case to ENG-4471 so the customer is notified when the fix ships.

## Backup policy

- Lumora takes encrypted snapshots of all workspace data **every 24 hours**, plus continuous transaction logs, in a separate region from production.
- **Retention:** 30 days (Starter, Team, Business). 90 days (Enterprise).
- Backups are for disaster recovery and restoring a whole workspace or project. They are not an archive the customer can browse.

|---|---|---|
| Deleted tasks, files, projects | **Trash** | 30 days |

Admins can add more people to these alerts: **Settings > Notifications > Workspace alerts > Storage**.

## What happens at 100%

New uploads and new file versions are blocked. Everything else, including viewing and downloading existing files, keeps working.

## Free up space

1. **Empty the trash.** Deleted files count until they are purged (30 days, or right away with **Empty trash**).

- Go to **Settings > Workspace > Custom domain** and enter a subdomain, e.g., `work.example.com`.
- In your DNS, create a **CNAME** record: `work.example.com → custom.lumora.example`.
- Click **Verify** — DNS propagation can take up to 24 hours, though it's usually much faster.
- Lumora automatically issues and renews the TLS certificate. If your domain has **CAA** records, you'll need to add `letsencrypt.org` to them.
- Once verified, the status shows **Active** and your old `lumora.example` address will redirect to the new custom domain.

A couple of related notes if you proceed with a subdomain:
- If you also use SAML SSO, you'll need to update your Identity Provider's Entity ID and ACS URL to the new domain — Lumora accepts both old and new addresses for 14 days during the transition.
- Webhook and API URLs do **not** change; the API stays on `api.lumora.example`.

Custom domains are an Enterprise-only feature — other plans use the `<subdomain>.lumora.example` format.

## Backup policy

- Lumora takes encrypted snapshots of all workspace data **every 24 hours**, plus continuous transaction logs, in a separate region from production.
- **Retention:** 30 days (Starter, Team, Business). 90 days (Enterprise).
- Backups are for disaster recovery and restoring a whole workspace or project. They are not an archive the customer can browse.

| Deleted tasks, files, projects | **Trash** | 30 days |
| Earlier versions of a file or document | **Version history** on the item | Depends on the version setting (KA-0016) |
| Deleted custom fields | **Settings > Fields > Deleted** | 30 days |
| Field changes on a task | **Activity** tab, then **Revert** | Unlimited |

4. **Compress or split** the file (for example a ZIP archive of the images).

article_number: KA-0032
title: Google Calendar two-way sync isn't working
url_name: google-calendar-sync
article_type: Troubleshooting
category: API & Integrations
plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-09-19
related_cases: [CASE-1016]
summary: How to fix Lumora events and task due dates not appearing in Google Calendar, or Google events not appearing in Lumora.
---

## How the sync works

- Each user connects their own Google account under **Profile > Integrations > Google Calendar**.
- **Lumora → Google:** tasks with a due date and time, and Lumora events, are written to one chosen calendar (by default a new calendar called *Lumora*).
- **Google → Lumora:** events from the calendars you tick show up on your Lumora calendar view.
- Changes usually sync within 2 minutes.

## Troubleshooting

1. **Looking at the wrong calendar.** Lumora items go to the *Lumora* calendar, not the user's primary calendar. In Google Calendar, make sure the *Lumora* calendar is visible (ticked in the left sidebar).
2. **Tasks without a time.** Tasks with only a due date are added as all-day events only if **Sync all-day tasks** is on.
3.

In Google Calendar, make sure the *Lumora* calendar is visible (ticked in the left sidebar).
2. **Tasks without a time.** Tasks with only a due date are added as all-day events only if **Sync all-day tasks** is on.
3. **Google calendars not ticked.** Under **Profile > Integrations > Google Calendar > Calendars to show**, tick the calendars that should appear in Lumora.
4. **Permission not granted.** If the user unticked calendar permissions on Google's consent screen, the sync works in only one direction. Disconnect, reconnect, and grant every requested permission.
5. **Google Workspace admin restrictions.** The customer's Google admin may block third-party apps. They need to allow *Lumora Workspace* under **Admin console > Security > API controls > App access control**.
6. **Token revoked.** A password change or Google security review can revoke access. The integration page then shows **Reconnect required**.

## Escalate

If the integration shows **Connected** and the steps above don't help, collect the user's email, an example item (its title and time, with timezone), and the direction of sync that fails. Escalate to the Integrations team.

| `Throttled by source (429)` | The *external system* is limiting Lumora's requests | Raise the API limit in the source system, or reduce the fields being synced |
| `Full resync in progress` | A schema change or a re-authorization started a full resync | Wait. Incremental syncs resume afterwards. Large sources can take hours |
| Runs are skipped or overlap | The previous sync hadn't finished when the next was due | Reduce the objects or fields synced, or ask for a longer interval |
| `Auth error` | The connection's credentials expired | Reconnect (see KA-0031 for Salesforce) |
| Nothing unusual, but runs are long | Possibly a backlog on Lumora's side | Check the status page, then escalate |

## Reduce sync volume

- Under **Connector > Objects**, turn off objects you don't use.
- Under **Connector > Filters**, sync only active records, for example `Status != Closed`.
- Avoid formula or rollup fields in the source system that change on every record each night. They make every record look modified.

## Escalate

Include the connector type, the workspace ID, and a screenshot or export of the sync log covering the slow period.

summary: Fixes for "Invalid verification code" when turning on or using 2FA, which is most often caused by the phone's clock being out of sync.
---

## Symptoms

The user scans the QR code in their authenticator app, types the 6-digit code, and sees **Invalid verification code**. This can happen during setup or at sign-in.

## Cause

Lumora uses time-based one-time passwords (TOTP, 30-second window, with a tolerance of one window either side). The usual causes are:

- **The phone's clock is wrong.** If it is more than about 60 seconds off, every code fails.
- **An old QR code was scanned.** Each time the setup dialog opens it creates a new secret, so a code from a previous attempt won't work.
- **The code was entered after it expired.**

## Resolution

1. On the phone, turn on automatic date and time:

## Step 3: Customer-side checks

1. Open `https://lumora.example/speedtest`, which measures latency to the nearest Lumora region.
2. Try a private browser window with extensions turned off. Ad blockers and some security extensions slow down the app considerably.
3. Make sure the corporate proxy allows WebSockets to `rt.lumora.example`. Without them the app falls back to slower polling (KA-0029).
4. Check the browser is supported and the device has at least 8 GB of RAM if it opens boards with thousands of cards.

## Step 4: Workspace-side checks (agent)

In the Support Console, open **Workspace > Health**:

- **Automation runs per hour.** Bulk automations scheduled at a fixed time can slow down that workspace. Suggest spreading them out.
- **Connector syncs.** Large full syncs can be moved to off-peak hours.

## Step 5: Escalate with data

Include the workspace ID, the affected users, time windows **with timezone**, speed test results, and a HAR file captured while the app was slow (KA-0003).

## Resolution

1. Update to **2.3.2 or later** from the App Store.
2. If the App Store doesn't offer the update yet, delete and reinstall the app. Offline data that hasn't synced will be lost. Data already synced is safe on the server.
3. Users whose company manages iOS devices (MDM) may need IT to push the update.

## Workaround if updating isn't possible

Use the mobile web version at `https://app.lumora.example` in Safari until the update is installed.

## Agent notes

If a user still reports a crash on launch with 2.3.2 or later, this article doesn't apply. Ask for the app version, the iOS version, and the crash log (**Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements > Analytics Data**, entries starting with `Lumora`), then escalate to Mobile Engineering.

article_number: KA-0018
title: API rate limits and handling HTTP 429 responses
url_name: api-rate-limits
article_type: Reference
category: API & Integrations
plans: [Team, Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-10-08
related_cases: [CASE-1025]
summary: How Lumora API rate limits are counted (per workspace, across all tokens and integrations), which response headers to read, and how to avoid 429 errors.
---

## How limits are counted

Limits apply **per workspace per minute**, shared by **every** API token and installed integration in that workspace. This is the most common reason a customer says "we're hitting the limit even though we're within it": their own integration is sharing the allowance with other apps, such as the Salesforce connector, Zapier-style tools or a BI connector.

| Plan | Requests per minute | Burst |
|---|---|---|
| Team | 100 | 20 |
| Business | 300 | 50 |
| Enterprise | 1,000 | 200 |

Search endpoints (`/v2/search`) have a separate limit of 30 per minute on every plan.

## Response headers

Every response includes:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: the workspace's allowance
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: requests left in the current window

summary: Changes from other users showing up about 30 seconds late almost always means WebSockets are blocked and the app has fallen back to polling. Here is how to confirm and fix it.
---

## Symptoms

When several people edit the same board, document or task at once, each person's changes reach the others about **30 seconds** late instead of immediately. Users may also see edit conflicts.

## Cause

Lumora sends live updates over a WebSocket connection to `wss://rt.lumora.example`. If something on the network blocks or breaks WebSockets, the app quietly falls back to **polling every 30 seconds**. That matches the delay users describe. Common culprits:

- A corporate proxy or secure web gateway that doesn't support WebSocket upgrades, or that inspects TLS traffic.
- A firewall that closes idle connections after a short time.
- Browser extensions (privacy or ad-blocking tools).

## Confirm

1. In the app, open **Help > Connection diagnostics**.

## Backup policy

- Lumora takes encrypted snapshots of all workspace data **every 24 hours**, plus continuous transaction logs, in a separate region from production.
- **Retention:** 30 days (Starter, Team, Business). 90 days (Enterprise).
- Backups are for disaster recovery and restoring a whole workspace or project. They are not an archive the customer can browse.

## What users can restore themselves

| What | Where | How long |
|---|---|---|
| Deleted tasks, files, projects | **Trash** | 30 days |
| Earlier versions of a file or document | **Version history** on the item | Depends on the version setting (KA-0016) |
| Deleted custom fields | **Settings > Fields > Deleted** | 30 days |
| Field changes on a task | **Activity** tab, then **Revert** | Unlimited |

4. Team and Business include 5 free guests per paid seat.

Limitations: guests don't see your member directory, can't create projects, and see their tasks from your workspace separately from their own.

## Enterprise Organizations

An **Organization** groups several Enterprise workspaces under one admin console.

1. An Organization Admin turns on **Org settings > Collaboration > Shared projects**.
2. In any workspace, a project manager clicks **Project > ⋯ > Share with workspaces** and chooses the target workspaces.
3. Members of those workspaces see the project in their own sidebar with their normal role, without becoming guests.
4. Reports and dashboards can include shared projects. Automations run in the workspace that **owns** the project.

## Limitations

- Shared projects can't be moved between workspaces. Ownership stays with the original workspace.
- Custom fields only from the owning workspace appear in a shared project.
- To combine two workspaces permanently, ask Support for a **workspace merge** (Enterprise, planned with the CSM).

## Requesting a restore from backup

For anything not covered above (for example a project bulk-edited by mistake, or data deleted more than 30 days ago but still within the backup window):

1. A workspace **Owner** must ask for it in writing on the case.
2. Give the project or workspace name and a point in time (date, time and timezone) to restore to.
3. Restores are done **into a new copy of the project**, never over live data. The customer then copies back what they need.
4. Target time: 2 business days (Enterprise: 1 business day). There is no charge on Business and Enterprise. On Starter and Team, the first restore each year is free.

## Customer-side backups

## What happens when payment fails?

1. **Days 0–14 (grace period):** Everything works. A banner is shown to Owners.
2. **After day 14:** The workspace becomes **read-only** for everyone except Owners, who can still reach billing.
3. **After day 60:** The workspace is suspended. Data is kept for 90 more days, then deleted.

## Restore access

An Owner updates the payment method under **Settings > Billing > Payment method** and clicks **Retry payment**. Access comes back within a minute of a successful charge.

- **Medium**: A feature misbehaves but a reasonable workaround exists, or the customer has a how-to question that blocks them.
- **Low**: General questions, feature requests, cosmetic issues.

article_number: KA-0007
title: Setting up SAML single sign-on
url_name: configure-saml-sso
article_type: How-to
category: Sign-in & Security
plans: [Business, Enterprise]
last_reviewed: 2026-09-18
related_cases: [CASE-1018]
summary: How to connect Lumora Workspace to a SAML 2.0 identity provider (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace and others), with fixes for the most common setup errors.
---

## Before you start

- You need Business or Enterprise, and the workspace **Owner** role.
- Claim and verify your email domain first: **Settings > Security > Domains**. You verify it with a DNS TXT record.

## Values to enter in your IdP

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Entity ID / Audience URI | `https://<subdomain>.lumora.example/sso/saml/metadata` |
| ACS (Reply) URL | `https://<subdomain>.lumora.example/sso/saml/acs` |
| Single Logout URL (optional) | `https://<subdomain>.lumora.example/sso/saml/slo` |
| NameID format | `emailAddress` |
| Required attributes | `email`, `firstName`, `lastName` |

## Steps in Lumora

1. If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL**, Lumora never hears about the IdP logout. The Lumora session lasts until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
2. Even when Single Logout is set up, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout. This is the defect being fixed in 2026.11.1.

## Workarounds

1. Make sure Single Logout is configured in **both** the IdP and in Lumora (**Settings > Security > Single sign-on > Edit > Single Logout URL**). This ends the server-side session.
2. Shorten **Settings > Security > Session lifetime** to as little as 1 hour.
3. On shared or kiosk devices, turn on **Settings > Security > Disable offline cache**. Users lose offline access, but nothing is cached on the device.
4. Users can sign out with **Profile > Sign out** in Lumora as well as in the IdP. That clears the local cache.

## Customer messaging

Tell customers that server-side sessions **are** ended when Single Logout is configured. The remaining risk is data cached in the browser on that device. Link the case to ENG-4471 so the customer is notified when the fix ships.

## Status

**Open.** Engineering ticket ENG-4471. Fix planned for release **2026.11.1**.

## Symptoms

- A user logs out through their identity provider portal (IdP-initiated logout), but Lumora tabs that are already open keep working.

## Cause

There are two separate problems:

1. If the SAML connection has no **Single Logout URL**, Lumora never hears about the IdP logout. The Lumora session lasts until it times out on its own (12 hours by default).
2. Even when Single Logout is set up, the web app's offline cache (service worker) isn't cleared on logout.

**SSO is enforced.** If the workspace requires SSO, Lumora does not send reset emails, because the password is managed by the identity provider. The user should sign in with **Continue with SSO** and reset their password through their company IdP.

4. **Typo or a different account email.** Confirm the exact email on the user record. Plus-addressing (`name+tag@`) is treated as a separate address.
5. **Rate limit.** The sign-in page sends at most 3 reset emails per address per hour. Ask the user to wait for the latest email and not keep clicking.

## Still not working

An Admin can send a reset link from **Settings > Members > ⋯ > Send password reset**. If that email doesn't arrive either, escalate to the Messaging team with the user's email address and the time of the attempt in UTC.

## Status

**Resolved** in Lumora for iOS **2.3.2** (released 2026-07-15). Ticket MOB-982.

## Symptoms

- The iOS app closes straight after the splash screen.
- Affects version **2.3.1** on iOS 17 and 18, but only for users who had **offline mode** turned on.

## Cause

A database migration in 2.3.1 failed on devices that already had offline data stored, and the app crashed every time it started.

## Resolution

1. Update to **2.3.2 or later** from the App Store.
2. If the App Store doesn't offer the update yet, delete and reinstall the app.

## Resolution

1. Update to **2.3.2 or later** from the App Store.
2. If the App Store doesn't offer the update yet, delete and reinstall the app. Offline data that hasn't synced will be lost. Data already synced is safe on the server.
3. Users whose company manages iOS devices (MDM) may need IT to push the update.

## Workaround if updating isn't possible

Use the mobile web version at `https://app.lumora.example` in Safari until the update is installed.

## Agent notes

If a user still reports a crash on launch with 2.3.2 or later, this article doesn't apply. Ask for the app version, the iOS version, and the crash log (**Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements > Analytics Data**, entries starting with `Lumora`), then escalate to Mobile Engineering.

- **Urgent**: Production is down or unusable for most users, or payments/data integrity are affected, with no workaround. Examples: the mobile app crashes on launch for all users, the payment gateway is failing, invitation emails stop going out to everyone.
- **High**: A major feature is broken or badly degraded and the workaround is painful. Examples: webhooks returning 500, exports coming out empty, sensitive data appearing in exports.
- **Medium**: A feature misbehaves but a reasonable workaround exists, or the customer has a how-to question that blocks them.
- **Low**: General questions, feature requests, cosmetic issues.

Agents may change the priority the customer picked, and must add a case comment explaining why.

## First-response targets (Business and Enterprise)

| Priority | Business | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|
| Urgent | 2 hours | 30 minutes |
| High | 4 hours | 2 hours |
| Medium | 1 business day | 8 hours |
| Low | 2 business days | 1 business day |

## Before you escalate

Attach the workspace ID, the affected user's email address, timestamps with timezone, and a HAR file for browser problems (see KA-0003).

| Team | Email, web form | Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00 ET |
| Business | Email, web form, chat | 24×5 |

## Priority definitions

- **Urgent**: Production is down or unusable for most users, or payments/data integrity are affected, with no workaround. Examples: the mobile app crashes on launch for all users, the payment gateway is failing, invitation emails stop going out to everyone.
- **High**: A major feature is broken or badly degraded and the workaround is painful. Examples: webhooks returning 500, exports coming out empty, sensitive data appearing in exports.

## Cause

The responsive layout treats screens between 1024 and 1366 px wide as desktop width but still applies the touch layout. The two clash.

## Workarounds

1. **Use the native app.** *Lumora for iPad* and the Android app have proper tablet layouts. This is the recommended option.
2. In Safari, tap **aA > Request Desktop Website**. The full desktop layout loads, with smaller touch targets.
3. Collapse the sidebar with the **«** button. It stays collapsed for the session.
4. Use portrait orientation.

## Agent notes

Link the case to FE-1290 so the customer is notified when the fix ships. Change the status to **Pending Release**, not Closed.

## Step 3: Customer-side checks

1. Open `https://lumora.example/speedtest`, which measures latency to the nearest Lumora region.
2. Try a private browser window with extensions turned off. Ad blockers and some security extensions slow down the app considerably.
3. Make sure the corporate proxy allows WebSockets to `rt.lumora.example`. Without them the app falls back to slower polling (KA-0029).
4. Check the browser is supported and the device has at least 8 GB of RAM if it opens boards with thousands of cards.

## Step 4: Workspace-side checks (agent)

In the Support Console, open **Workspace > Health**:

- **Automation runs per hour.** Bulk automations scheduled at a fixed time can slow down that workspace. Suggest spreading them out.
- **Connector syncs.** Large full syncs can be moved to off-peak hours.

## Step 5: Escalate with data

Include the workspace ID, the affected users, time windows **with timezone**, speed test results, and a HAR file captured while the app was slow (KA-0003).

## Dark mode

Dark mode arrived in release **2026.09.1** for the web and desktop apps. The mobile apps have had it since version 2.2.

**Web and desktop:** **Profile > Preferences > Appearance > Theme** gives three choices:

- **Light**
- **Dark**
- **Match system**, which follows the operating system's setting and switches automatically if the OS does (for example at sunset)

**iOS and Android:** **Settings > Appearance**. By default the app follows the device setting.

The setting is saved for each user and each device. Dashboards and charts switch to a dark-friendly color palette automatically.

## Other appearance settings

- **Density:** *Comfortable* or *Compact* rows in tables and boards.
- **High-contrast mode:** stronger borders and focus outlines (meets WCAG 2.2 AA).

## Firefox

1. Press **F12** and open **Network**. Tick **Persist Logs**.
2. Reproduce the problem.
3. Click the gear icon and choose **Save All As HAR**.

## Safari

1. Turn on **Develop** in **Settings > Advanced > Show features for web developers**.
2. Choose **Develop > Show Web Inspector > Network**, tick **Preserve Log**, and reproduce.
3. Click **Export**.

## Privacy

HAR files can contain session cookies. Ask customers to upload them through the secure attachment link on the case, never by email. Support deletes attachments 30 days after the case closes.

## Supported browsers

The latest two major versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. Internet Explorer and legacy Edge are not supported.
